\sphinxAtStartPar
py3plex provides scalable analysis and visualization of multilayer and multiplex networks in Python.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Key Features:}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Multiplex and multilayer network structures

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{SQL\sphinxhyphen{}like DSL for network queries} — first\sphinxhyphen{}class feature

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
17+ multilayer statistics and centrality measures

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Community detection (Louvain, Infomap, multilayer modularity)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Random walk algorithms (Node2Vec, DeepWalk) for embeddings

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Publication\sphinxhyphen{}ready visualizations

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
High\sphinxhyphen{}performance I/O with Arrow/Parquet support

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Full NetworkX compatibility

\end{itemize}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{DSL: Query Networks Like SQL}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The py3plex DSL lets you query networks using intuitive SQL\sphinxhyphen{}like syntax or a type\sphinxhyphen{}safe Python builder API:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{py3plex}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{dsl}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{execute\PYGZus{}query}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{Q}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{L}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} String DSL: Simple and readable}
\PYG{n}{result} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{execute\PYGZus{}query}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{,}
    \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{SELECT nodes WHERE layer=}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{social}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{ AND degree \PYGZgt{} 5 }\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}
    \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{COMPUTE betweenness\PYGZus{}centrality}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}
\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Builder API: Type\PYGZhy{}safe with autocompletion}
\PYG{n}{result} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{p}{(}
    \PYG{n}{Q}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{nodes}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{from\PYGZus{}layers}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{L}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{social}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{)}
     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{where}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{degree\PYGZus{}\PYGZus{}gt}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mi}{5}\PYG{p}{)}
     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{compute}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{betweenness\PYGZus{}centrality}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{order\PYGZus{}by}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZhy{}betweenness\PYGZus{}centrality}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{limit}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mi}{10}\PYG{p}{)}
     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{execute}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The DSL is \sphinxstylestrong{perfect for}:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Interactive network exploration

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Rapid prototyping

\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{add\PYGZus{}edges}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{[}

    \PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{Bob}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{friends}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{Carol}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{friends}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{,}
    \PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{Alice}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{colleagues}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{Bob}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{colleagues}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{input\PYGZus{}type}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{list}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{basic\PYGZus{}stats}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{visualize\PYGZus{}network}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{show}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{k+kc}{True}\PYG{p}{)}

\subsection{Overview}
\label{\detokenize{overview/part_intro:overview}}\label{\detokenize{overview/part_intro::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Welcome to py3plex! This section provides a high\sphinxhyphen{}level introduction to the library and its capabilities.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{What is py3plex?}

\sphinxAtStartPar
py3plex is a Python library for analyzing and visualizing multilayer and multiplex networks. Unlike traditional network analysis tools that treat all relationships uniformly, py3plex preserves the distinct types of connections between entities—whether they’re social ties, biological interactions, or transportation links.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Why py3plex?}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Native multilayer support:} Built from the ground up for networks with multiple relationship types

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{SQL\sphinxhyphen{}like DSL:} Query networks intuitively with SQL\sphinxhyphen{}inspired syntax

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Production\sphinxhyphen{}ready:} High\sphinxhyphen{}performance I/O, sklearn\sphinxhyphen{}style pipelines, and comprehensive testing

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Research\sphinxhyphen{}proven:} Used in multiple peer\sphinxhyphen{}reviewed publications

\subsection{What is py3plex?}
\label{\detokenize{overview/what_is_py3plex:what-is-py3plex}}\label{\detokenize{overview/what_is_py3plex::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
py3plex is a Python library for scalable analysis and visualization of multilayer and multiplex networks.


\subsubsection{Key Features}
\label{\detokenize{overview/what_is_py3plex:key-features}}

\paragraph{Multilayer Network Structures}
\label{\detokenize{overview/what_is_py3plex:multilayer-network-structures}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
py3plex provides native support for:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Multiplex networks} — Same nodes across multiple layers (e.g., social networks with friendship, collaboration, and family ties)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Heterogeneous networks} — Different node types across layers (e.g., author\sphinxhyphen{}paper\sphinxhyphen{}venue networks)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Temporal networks} — Networks that evolve over time with temporal attributes

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
All network types are first\sphinxhyphen{}class citizens with consistent APIs.


\paragraph{SQL\sphinxhyphen{}like DSL for Network Queries}
\label{\detokenize{overview/what_is_py3plex:sql-like-dsl-for-network-queries}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Query networks using intuitive SQL\sphinxhyphen{}inspired syntax:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{py3plex}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{dsl}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{execute\PYGZus{}query}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} String DSL: readable and concise}
\PYG{n}{result} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{execute\PYGZus{}query}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{,}
    \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{SELECT nodes WHERE layer=}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{social}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{ AND degree \PYGZgt{} 5 }\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}
    \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{COMPUTE betweenness\PYGZus{}centrality}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}
\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Or use the type\sphinxhyphen{}safe builder API:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{py3plex}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{dsl}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{Q}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{L}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Builder API: with IDE autocompletion}
\PYG{n}{result} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{p}{(}
    \PYG{n}{Q}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{nodes}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{from\PYGZus{}layers}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{L}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{social}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{)}
     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{where}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{degree\PYGZus{}\PYGZus{}gt}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mi}{5}\PYG{p}{)}
     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{compute}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{betweenness\PYGZus{}centrality}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{execute}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The DSL makes complex network analyses readable and maintainable.


\paragraph{Comprehensive Algorithm Suite}
\label{\detokenize{overview/what_is_py3plex:comprehensive-algorithm-suite}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
py3plex includes 17+ multilayer\sphinxhyphen{}specific algorithms:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Community detection:} Louvain, Infomap, multilayer modularity

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Centrality measures:} Multilayer PageRank, betweenness, versatility

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Random walks:} Node2Vec, DeepWalk for network embeddings

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Dynamics:} SIR/SIS epidemic models, diffusion processes

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
All algorithms handle multilayer structure natively without flattening.

\label{\detokenize{overview/what_is_py3plex:publication-ready-visualizations}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Create professional network diagrams with:

\sphinxAtStartPar
Automatic multilayer layouts

Customizable styling and colors

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Support for large networks (1000+ nodes)

\paragraph{High\sphinxhyphen{}Performance I/O}
\label{\detokenize{overview/what_is_py3plex:high-performance-i-o}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Apache Arrow/Parquet support for large datasets

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
NetworkX compatibility for easy integration

\sphinxAtStartPar
Multiple input formats (edge lists, adjacency matrices, JSON)

\end{itemize}


\subsubsection{What Makes py3plex Unique?}
\label{\detokenize{overview/what_is_py3plex:what-makes-py3plex-unique}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Native Multilayer Representation}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Unlike tools that flatten multilayer networks into single\sphinxhyphen{}layer graphs, py3plex preserves the multilayer structure throughout the analysis pipeline. This leads to more accurate results for multilayer\sphinxhyphen{}specific properties.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Node\sphinxhyphen{}Layer Pair Abstraction}

\sphinxAtStartPar
py3plex represents multilayer networks using node\sphinxhyphen{}layer pairs: a node in layer A is distinct from the same node in layer B. This clean abstraction enables:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Layer\sphinxhyphen{}specific queries

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Inter\sphinxhyphen{}layer and intra\sphinxhyphen{}layer edge differentiation

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Efficient supra\sphinxhyphen{}adjacency matrix operations

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Production\sphinxhyphen{}Ready Design}

\sphinxAtStartPar
py3plex is designed for both research and production:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Sklearn\sphinxhyphen{}style pipelines for reproducible workflows

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Comprehensive type hints and documentation

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Extensive test suite (500+ tests)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
CLI and Docker deployment options

\end{itemize}


\subsubsection{When to Use py3plex?}
\label{\detokenize{overview/what_is_py3plex:when-to-use-py3plex}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
py3plex is ideal when you have:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Multiple relationship types} between entities (e.g., email + phone + in\sphinxhyphen{}person contacts)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Heterogeneous networks} with different node types (e.g., users, posts, hashtags)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Temporal networks} where relationships change over time

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Need for layer\sphinxhyphen{}specific analysis} (e.g., comparing community structure across layers)

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
If you only need single\sphinxhyphen{}layer network analysis, NetworkX or igraph might be simpler choices.


\subsubsection{Related Projects}
\label{\detokenize{overview/what_is_py3plex:related-projects}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{NetworkX:} py3plex builds on NetworkX for single\sphinxhyphen{}layer operations

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{igraph:} Faster for single\sphinxhyphen{}layer networks, but limited multilayer support

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{pymnet:} Pure Python multilayer library, different API design

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{graph\sphinxhyphen{}tool:} High performance, but steeper learning curve

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
py3plex balances ease of use with multilayer\sphinxhyphen{}specific functionality.

\subsection{Multilayer Networks in 2 Minutes}
\label{\detokenize{overview/multilayer_in_2min:multilayer-networks-in-2-minutes}}\label{\detokenize{overview/multilayer_in_2min::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
A \sphinxstylestrong{multilayer network} represents systems where entities can be connected through multiple types of relationships simultaneously.


\subsubsection{The Core Idea}
\label{\detokenize{overview/multilayer_in_2min:the-core-idea}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
In the real world, relationships are rarely uniform. Consider a group of researchers:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
They \sphinxstylestrong{co\sphinxhyphen{}author papers} (collaboration network)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
They \sphinxstylestrong{cite each other} (citation network)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
They \sphinxstylestrong{attend conferences} together (social network)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
They may \sphinxstylestrong{share funding} (grant network)

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
A single\sphinxhyphen{}layer network can only capture one of these relationships. A multilayer network captures all of them.


\subsubsection{Visual Intuition}
\label{\detokenize{overview/multilayer_in_2min:visual-intuition}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
Single\PYGZhy{}layer network (e.g., only co\PYGZhy{}authorship):

Alice \PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{} Bob \PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{} Carol
          |
        David

Multilayer network (co\PYGZhy{}authorship + citations):

Layer 1 (Co\PYGZhy{}authorship):
Alice \PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{} Bob \PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{} Carol
          |
        David

Layer 2 (Citations):
Alice \PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZgt{} Bob \PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZgt{} Carol
          ↓
        David

Inter\PYGZhy{}layer connections:
Alice in Layer 1 ↔ Alice in Layer 2 (same person)
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsubsection{Key Concepts}
\label{\detokenize{overview/multilayer_in_2min:key-concepts}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Layers}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Each layer represents a type of relationship (e.g., friendship, collaboration, family).

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Intra\sphinxhyphen{}layer edges}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Connections within a single layer (e.g., Alice friends with Bob).

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Inter\sphinxhyphen{}layer edges}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Connections between layers, usually representing the same entity across layers (e.g., Alice in the friendship layer is the same person as Alice in the collaboration layer).

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Node\sphinxhyphen{}layer pairs}

\sphinxAtStartPar
In py3plex, a node in layer A is conceptually distinct from the same node in layer B. This is the fundamental abstraction that makes multilayer analysis possible.


\subsubsection{Types of Multilayer Networks}
\label{\detokenize{overview/multilayer_in_2min:types-of-multilayer-networks}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Multiplex networks}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Same nodes across all layers

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Different edge types per layer

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Example: Social media (same users, different platforms)

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Heterogeneous networks}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Different node types in different layers

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Example: Author\sphinxhyphen{}Paper\sphinxhyphen{}Venue networks

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Temporal networks}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Layers represent time slices

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Same nodes and edge types, but edges appear/disappear over time

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Example: Communication networks over days/weeks

\end{itemize}


\subsubsection{Why Multilayer Matters}
\label{\detokenize{overview/multilayer_in_2min:why-multilayer-matters}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Information is lost when flattening}

\sphinxAtStartPar
If you merge all layers into a single network, you lose critical information:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Which type of relationship connects two nodes?

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Are communities consistent across layers or layer\sphinxhyphen{}specific?

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
How do different relationship types interact?

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{New properties emerge}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Multilayer networks have properties that don’t exist in single\sphinxhyphen{}layer networks:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Node versatility:} How many layers does a node participate in?

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Layer correlation:} Are connections in layer A predictive of layer B?

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Multilayer communities:} Groups that span multiple relationship types

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Multiplexity:} Number of different relationship types between two nodes

\end{itemize}


\subsubsection{Real\sphinxhyphen{}World Impact}
\label{\detokenize{overview/multilayer_in_2min:real-world-impact}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Example: Disease spread}

\sphinxAtStartPar
In epidemic modeling, people interact through:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Household contacts (high transmission rate)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Workplace contacts (medium rate, large reach)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Social gatherings (variable)

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
A single\sphinxhyphen{}layer model that averages these interactions will give incorrect predictions. A multilayer model preserves the structure and transmission dynamics of each contact type.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Example: Social influence}

\sphinxAtStartPar
A person might be influential on Twitter (many followers) but not on LinkedIn (few connections). Flattening these into a single “social network” loses this nuance.

\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{input\PYGZus{}type}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{list}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Analyze}

\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+sa}{f}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{Edges: }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n}{stats}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{edges}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}

\subsubsection{When to Use Multilayer Analysis?}
\label{\detokenize{overview/multilayer_in_2min:when-to-use-multilayer-analysis}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Use multilayer networks when:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
✅ You have \sphinxstylestrong{multiple relationship types} between entities

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
✅ The \sphinxstylestrong{type of relationship matters} for your analysis

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
✅ You want to \sphinxstylestrong{preserve layer\sphinxhyphen{}specific structure}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
✅ You’re studying \sphinxstylestrong{cross\sphinxhyphen{}layer effects} (e.g., how Twitter activity affects LinkedIn connections)

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Stick with single\sphinxhyphen{}layer when:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
❌ All relationships are of the same type

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
❌ Relationship type doesn’t affect your analysis

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
❌ You only care about aggregate connectivity

\end{itemize}

\subsubsection{Basic Installation}
\label{\detokenize{getting_started/installation:basic-installation}}

\paragraph{Install from GitHub (Recommended)}
\label{\detokenize{getting_started/installation:install-from-github-recommended}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The latest version is always available on GitHub:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
pip\PYG{+w}{ }install\PYG{+w}{ }py3plex
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
This installs the core py3plex library with all required dependencies.


\paragraph{Install from Source}
\label{\detokenize{getting_started/installation:install-from-source}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
For development or to access the latest features:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
git\PYG{+w}{ }clone\PYG{+w}{ }https://github.com/SkBlaz/py3plex.git
\PYG{n+nb}{cd}\PYG{+w}{ }py3plex
pip\PYG{+w}{ }install\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}e\PYG{+w}{ }.
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}e}} flag installs in editable mode, so changes to the source code are immediately available.


\paragraph{Docker Installation (Alternative)}
\label{\detokenize{getting_started/installation:docker-installation-alternative}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
For a containerized environment with all dependencies pre\sphinxhyphen{}installed, use Docker:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Clone the repository}
git\PYG{+w}{ }clone\PYG{+w}{ }https://github.com/SkBlaz/py3plex.git
\PYG{n+nb}{cd}\PYG{+w}{ }py3plex

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Build the Docker image}
docker\PYG{+w}{ }build\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}t\PYG{+w}{ }py3plex:latest\PYG{+w}{ }.

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Run py3plex commands}
docker\PYG{+w}{ }run\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}rm\PYG{+w}{ }py3plex:latest\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}version
docker\PYG{+w}{ }run\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}rm\PYG{+w}{ }py3plex:latest\PYG{+w}{ }selftest
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Benefits of Docker installation:}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
No Python environment setup required

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
All dependencies pre\sphinxhyphen{}installed and tested

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Consistent environment across different systems

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Isolated from system Python installation

\end{itemize}

See {\hyperref[\detokenize{deployment/cli_and_docker::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Docker Usage Guide}}}} for complete Docker documentation including:

Docker Compose usage

Helper scripts (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{py3plex\sphinxhyphen{}docker.sh}})

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Batch processing and CI/CD integration

\end{itemize}


\subsubsection{Optional Dependencies}
\label{\detokenize{getting_started/installation:optional-dependencies}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
py3plex offers several optional feature sets that can be installed separately:


\paragraph{Advanced Community Detection}
\label{\detokenize{getting_started/installation:advanced-community-detection}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Install Infomap for advanced overlapping community detection:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
pip\PYG{+w}{ }install\PYG{+w}{ }py3plex\PYG{o}{[}infomap\PYG{o}{]}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\paragraph{Additional Algorithms}
\label{\detokenize{getting_started/installation:additional-algorithms}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Install extra community detection algorithms (Louvain, cdlib):

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
pip\PYG{+w}{ }install\PYG{+w}{ }py3plex\PYG{o}{[}algos\PYG{o}{]}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\paragraph{Advanced Visualization}
\label{\detokenize{getting_started/installation:advanced-visualization}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Install Plotly and igraph for interactive and advanced visualizations:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
pip\PYG{+w}{ }install\PYG{+w}{ }py3plex\PYG{o}{[}viz\PYG{o}{]}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\paragraph{Apache Arrow Support}
\label{\detokenize{getting_started/installation:apache-arrow-support}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Install pyarrow for high\sphinxhyphen{}performance I/O with Arrow/Parquet formats:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
pip\PYG{+w}{ }install\PYG{+w}{ }py3plex\PYG{o}{[}arrow\PYG{o}{]}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Arrow format provides 2\sphinxhyphen{}3x faster read/write operations and better compression compared to JSON.
See \DUrole{xref}{\DUrole{std}{\DUrole{std-doc}{../user\_guide/io\_and\_formats}}} for details on using Arrow format.


\paragraph{Multiple Extras}
\label{\detokenize{getting_started/installation:multiple-extras}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Install multiple feature sets at once:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
pip\PYG{+w}{ }install\PYG{+w}{ }py3plex\PYG{o}{[}infomap,viz,algos,arrow\PYG{o}{]}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\paragraph{Development Installation}
\label{\detokenize{getting_started/installation:development-installation}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
For contributors, install with development tools (testing, linting):

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Recommended (Makefile\sphinxhyphen{}based):}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
git\PYG{+w}{ }clone\PYG{+w}{ }https://github.com/SkBlaz/py3plex.git
\PYG{n+nb}{cd}\PYG{+w}{ }py3plex
make\PYG{+w}{ }setup\PYG{+w}{        }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Create virtual environment}
make\PYG{+w}{ }dev\PYGZhy{}install\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Install with dev dependencies}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Alternative (manual):}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
git\PYG{+w}{ }clone\PYG{+w}{ }https://github.com/SkBlaz/py3plex.git
\PYG{n+nb}{cd}\PYG{+w}{ }py3plex
pip\PYG{+w}{ }install\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}e\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}.[dev]\PYGZdq{}}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Both methods install:

\label{\detokenize{getting_started/installation:infomap-community-detection}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
For advanced community detection using Infomap:

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Option 1:} Use the bundled Python implementation (recommended):

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]

\sphinxAtStartPar
Follow platform\sphinxhyphen{}specific installation instructions

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Alternative:} Use the built\sphinxhyphen{}in Louvain algorithm (no binary needed):

\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\label{\detokenize{getting_started/installation:node2vec-embeddings}}

For Node2Vec node embeddings, use pure Python alternatives:

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Option 1:} Use pecanpy (fast parallel implementation):

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Option 2:} Use node2vec package:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
pip\PYG{+w}{ }install\PYG{+w}{ }node2vec
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Option 3:} Use py3plex’s built\sphinxhyphen{}in random walk implementation:

\PYG{n}{walks} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{generate\PYGZus{}walks}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{core\PYGZus{}network}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{num\PYGZus{}walks}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mi}{10}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{walk\PYGZus{}length}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mi}{80}\PYG{p}{)}

\subsubsection{Virtual Environment Setup}
\label{\detokenize{getting_started/installation:virtual-environment-setup}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
We strongly recommend using a virtual environment:


\paragraph{Using venv}
\label{\detokenize{getting_started/installation:using-venv}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Create virtual environment}
python3\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}m\PYG{+w}{ }venv\PYG{+w}{ }py3plex\PYGZhy{}env

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Activate (Linux/macOS)}
\PYG{n+nb}{source}\PYG{+w}{ }py3plex\PYGZhy{}env/bin/activate

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Activate (Windows)}
py3plex\PYGZhy{}env\PYG{l+s+se}{\PYGZbs{}S}cripts\PYG{l+s+se}{\PYGZbs{}a}ctivate

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Install py3plex}
pip\PYG{+w}{ }install\PYG{+w}{ }py3plex
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\paragraph{Using conda}
\label{\detokenize{getting_started/installation:using-conda}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Create conda environment}
conda\PYG{+w}{ }create\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}n\PYG{+w}{ }py3plex\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nv}{python}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m}{3}.10

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Activate}
conda\PYG{+w}{ }activate\PYG{+w}{ }py3plex

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Install py3plex}
pip\PYG{+w}{ }install\PYG{+w}{ }py3plex
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsubsection{Common Installation Issues}
\label{\detokenize{getting_started/installation:common-installation-issues}}

\paragraph{Issue: “No module named ‘numpy’”}
\label{\detokenize{getting_started/installation:issue-no-module-named-numpy}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Solution:} Install numpy first:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
pip\PYG{+w}{ }install\PYG{+w}{ }numpy
pip\PYG{+w}{ }install\PYG{+w}{ }py3plex
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\paragraph{Issue: Compilation errors on Windows}
\label{\detokenize{getting_started/installation:issue-compilation-errors-on-windows}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Solution:} Install Visual C++ Build Tools:
\begin{enumerate}
\sphinxsetlistlabels{\arabic}{enumi}{enumii}{}{.}%
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Download from: \sphinxurl{https://visualstudio.microsoft.com/visual-cpp-build-tools/}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Install “Desktop development with C++”

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Retry installation

\end{enumerate}


\paragraph{Issue: “Permission denied” on Linux/macOS}
\label{\detokenize{getting_started/installation:issue-permission-denied-on-linux-macos}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Solution:} Use pip install with \textendash{}user flag:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
pip\PYG{+w}{ }install\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}user\PYG{+w}{ }py3plex
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Or use a virtual environment (recommended).


\paragraph{Issue: Old version installed}
\label{\detokenize{getting_started/installation:issue-old-version-installed}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Solution:} Upgrade to latest version:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
pip\PYG{+w}{ }install\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}upgrade\PYG{+w}{ }py3plex
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\subsection{10\sphinxhyphen{}Minute Tutorial}
\label{\detokenize{getting_started/tutorial_10min:minute-tutorial}}\label{\detokenize{getting_started/tutorial_10min::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Create a multilayer network, compute statistics, detect communities, and visualize—all in 10 minutes. This comprehensive tutorial takes you from basic network creation to advanced multilayer analysis.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{You will learn:}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Create multilayer networks from scratch and load from files

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Display network statistics and understand the multilayer model

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Compute layer\sphinxhyphen{}specific and multilayer metrics

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Query networks with the SQL\sphinxhyphen{}like DSL

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Detect communities across layers

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Generate random walks for embeddings

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Create publication\sphinxhyphen{}ready visualizations

\end{itemize}


\subsubsection{Installation}
\label{\detokenize{getting_started/tutorial_10min:installation}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
pip\PYG{+w}{ }install\PYG{+w}{ }py3plex
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
For Docker setup or optional dependencies, see {\hyperref[\detokenize{getting_started/installation::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Installation and Setup}}}}.


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip



\subsubsection{Part 1: Your First Network (2 min)}
\label{\detokenize{getting_started/tutorial_10min:part-1-your-first-network-2-min}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Let’s create a simple multilayer network and explore its basic properties.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Create from scratch:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{py3plex}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{core}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{multinet}

\PYG{n}{network} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{multinet}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{multi\PYGZus{}layer\PYGZus{}network}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Format: [source\PYGZus{}node, source\PYGZus{}layer, target\PYGZus{}node, target\PYGZus{}layer, weight]}
\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{add\PYGZus{}edges}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{[}
    \PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{Alice}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{friends}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{Bob}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{friends}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{,}
    \PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{Bob}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{friends}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{Carol}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{friends}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{,}
    \PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{Alice}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{colleagues}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{Bob}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{colleagues}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{,}
    \PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{Bob}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{colleagues}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{Dave}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{colleagues}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{p}{]}
\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{input\PYGZus{}type}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{list}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{basic\PYGZus{}stats}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Output:}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
Number of nodes: 6
Number of edges: 4
Number of unique nodes (as node\PYGZhy{}layer tuples): 6
Number of unique node IDs (across all layers): 4
Nodes per layer:
  Layer \PYGZsq{}friends\PYGZsq{}: 3 nodes
  Layer \PYGZsq{}colleagues\PYGZsq{}: 3 nodes
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Key concept:} The network has 6 node\sphinxhyphen{}layer pairs but only 4 unique people. Alice appears in both layers as \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{(\textquotesingle{}Alice\textquotesingle{}, \textquotesingle{}friends\textquotesingle{})}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{(\textquotesingle{}Alice\textquotesingle{}, \textquotesingle{}colleagues\textquotesingle{})}}.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Visualize your network:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{py3plex}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{visualization}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{multilayer}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{draw\PYGZus{}multilayer\PYGZus{}default}

\PYG{n}{draw\PYGZus{}multilayer\PYGZus{}default}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{display}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{k+kc}{True}\PYG{p}{)}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]

\PYG{n}{network} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{multinet}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{multi\PYGZus{}layer\PYGZus{}network}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{load\PYGZus{}network}\PYG{p}{(}

    \PYG{n}{directed}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{k+kc}{False}  \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Set to True for directed networks}
\PYG{p}{)}

\subsubsection{Part 2: Basic Analysis (2 min)}
\label{\detokenize{getting_started/tutorial_10min:part-2-basic-analysis-2-min}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Compute layer\sphinxhyphen{}specific metrics:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{py3plex}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{algorithms}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{statistics}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{multilayer\PYGZus{}statistics} \PYG{k}{as} \PYG{n}{mls}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Layer density: how connected is each layer?}
\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+sa}{f}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{Friends density: }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n}{mls}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{layer\PYGZus{}density}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{friends}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{l+s+si}{:}\PYG{l+s+s2}{.3f}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+sa}{f}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{Colleagues density: }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n}{mls}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{layer\PYGZus{}density}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{colleagues}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{l+s+si}{:}\PYG{l+s+s2}{.3f}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Node activity: what fraction of layers does Bob appear in?}
\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+sa}{f}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{Bob}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{s activity: }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n}{mls}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{node\PYGZus{}activity}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{Bob}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{l+s+si}{:}\PYG{l+s+s2}{.3f}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Output:}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
Friends density: 0.667
Colleagues density: 0.667
Bob\PYGZsq{}s activity: 1.000

\subsubsection{Key Concepts}
\label{\detokenize{getting_started/tutorial_10min:key-concepts}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Understanding these core concepts will help you work effectively with py3plex:
\begin{enumerate}
\sphinxsetlistlabels{\arabic}{enumi}{enumii}{}{.}%
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Node\sphinxhyphen{}layer pairs:} Nodes are \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{(node\_id, layer\_id)}} tuples. Alice in friends is different from Alice in colleagues. This allows the same entity to have different connections in different contexts.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Layers preserve context:} Each layer represents a different relationship type (friends, colleagues, family, etc.). Statistics and algorithms respect layer boundaries, revealing patterns invisible to single\sphinxhyphen{}layer analysis.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{NetworkX compatible:} py3plex uses NetworkX internally. All NetworkX algorithms work on py3plex networks, giving you access to a rich ecosystem of graph algorithms.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Multilayer statistics:} Metrics like node activity and edge overlap reveal cross\sphinxhyphen{}layer patterns. These measures quantify how entities interact across different relationship contexts.

\end{enumerate}


\bigskip\hrule\bigskip

\PYG{p}{)}

\subsection{Common Issues and Troubleshooting}
\label{\detokenize{getting_started/common_issues:common-issues-and-troubleshooting}}\label{\detokenize{getting_started/common_issues::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This guide helps you troubleshoot common problems when getting started with py3plex.


\subsubsection{Installation Issues}
\label{\detokenize{getting_started/common_issues:installation-issues}}

\paragraph{“No module named ‘numpy’”}
\label{\detokenize{getting_started/common_issues:no-module-named-numpy}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Problem:} Import error when trying to use py3plex.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Solution:} Install numpy first:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
pip\PYG{+w}{ }install\PYG{+w}{ }numpy
pip\PYG{+w}{ }install\PYG{+w}{ }py3plex
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\paragraph{Compilation Errors on Windows}
\label{\detokenize{getting_started/common_issues:compilation-errors-on-windows}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Problem:} C++ compilation errors during installation on Windows.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Solution:} Install Visual C++ Build Tools:
\begin{enumerate}
\sphinxsetlistlabels{\arabic}{enumi}{enumii}{}{.}%
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Download from: \sphinxurl{https://visualstudio.microsoft.com/visual-cpp-build-tools/}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Install “Desktop development with C++”

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Retry installation

\end{enumerate}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
pip\PYG{+w}{ }install\PYG{+w}{ }py3plex
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\paragraph{“Permission denied” on Linux/macOS}
\label{\detokenize{getting_started/common_issues:permission-denied-on-linux-macos}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Problem:} Permission errors during pip install.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Solution 1:} Use pip install with \textendash{}user flag:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
pip\PYG{+w}{ }install\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}user\PYG{+w}{ }py3plex
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Solution 2:} Use a virtual environment (recommended):

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
python3\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}m\PYG{+w}{ }venv\PYG{+w}{ }py3plex\PYGZhy{}env
\PYG{n+nb}{source}\PYG{+w}{ }py3plex\PYGZhy{}env/bin/activate\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} On Windows: py3plex\PYGZhy{}env\PYGZbs{}Scripts\PYGZbs{}activate}
pip\PYG{+w}{ }install\PYG{+w}{ }py3plex
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\paragraph{Old Version Installed}
\label{\detokenize{getting_started/common_issues:old-version-installed}}
\sphinxAtStartPar

\sphinxstylestrong{Problem:} Loading large networks takes too long.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Solution 1:} Use Arrow/Parquet format for large networks:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{py3plex}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{io}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{read}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{write}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Load much faster}
\PYG{n}{network} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{read}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{network.arrow}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Solution 2:} Process in chunks or use subnetworks:

\sphinxAtStartPar

\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Try different resolution parameters}

    \PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{,}
    \PYG{n}{gamma}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mf}{0.5}\PYG{p}{,}    \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Lower = fewer, larger communities}
    \PYG{n}{omega}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mf}{1.5}\PYG{p}{,}    \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Higher = more layer consistency}
    \PYG{n}{random\PYGZus{}state}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mi}{42}
\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

    \PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{key}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{n+nb}{len}\PYG{p}{)}

\paragraph{Method 1: Add Edges Directly (Recommended)}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/load_and_build_networks:method-1-add-edges-directly-recommended}}
\sphinxAtStartPar

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Add edges in list format}
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Format: [source\PYGZus{}node, source\PYGZus{}layer, target\PYGZus{}node, target\PYGZus{}layer, weight]}
\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{add\PYGZus{}edges}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{[}
    \PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{Alice}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{friends}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{Bob}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{friends}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mf}{1.0}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{,}
    \PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{Bob}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{friends}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{Carol}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{friends}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mf}{1.0}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{,}
    \PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{Alice}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{colleagues}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{Bob}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{colleagues}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mf}{1.0}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{,}
    \PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{Bob}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{colleagues}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{Dave}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{colleagues}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mf}{1.0}\PYG{p}{]}
\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{input\PYGZus{}type}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{list}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}

    \PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{Alice}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{colleagues}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{,}

\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Add edges between existing nodes}

\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{basic\PYGZus{}stats}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}

\subsubsection{Layer\sphinxhyphen{}Specific Statistics}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/compute_statistics:layer-specific-statistics}}

\paragraph{Compute Per\sphinxhyphen{}Layer Density}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/compute_statistics:compute-per-layer-density}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{layers} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{get\PYGZus{}layers}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{k}{for} \PYG{n}{layer} \PYG{o+ow}{in} \PYG{n}{layers}\PYG{p}{:}
    \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Get nodes and edges in this layer}
    \PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{py3plex}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{dsl}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{Q}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{L}

    \PYG{n}{nodes} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{Q}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{nodes}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{from\PYGZus{}layers}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{L}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{n}{layer}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{execute}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{)}
    \PYG{n}{edges} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{Q}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{edges}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{from\PYGZus{}layers}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{L}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{n}{layer}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{execute}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{)}

    \PYG{n}{n} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n+nb}{len}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{nodes}\PYG{p}{)}
    \PYG{n}{m} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n+nb}{len}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{edges}\PYG{p}{)}

    \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Density = actual edges / possible edges}
    \PYG{n}{max\PYGZus{}edges} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{n} \PYG{o}{*} \PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{n} \PYG{o}{\PYGZhy{}} \PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{p}{)} \PYG{o}{/} \PYG{l+m+mi}{2}  \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} undirected}
    \PYG{n}{density} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{m} \PYG{o}{/} \PYG{n}{max\PYGZus{}edges} \PYG{k}{if} \PYG{n}{max\PYGZus{}edges} \PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}} \PYG{l+m+mi}{0} \PYG{k}{else} \PYG{l+m+mi}{0}

    \PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+sa}{f}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{Layer }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n}{layer}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{: density = }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n}{density}\PYG{l+s+si}{:}\PYG{l+s+s2}{.4f}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\paragraph{Compare Layers}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/compute_statistics:compare-layers}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Use the DSL for efficient comparison:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{py3plex}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{dsl}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{Q}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{L}

\PYG{k}{for} \PYG{n}{layer} \PYG{o+ow}{in} \PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{layer1}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{layer2}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{layer3}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{:}
    \PYG{n}{result} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{p}{(}
        \PYG{n}{Q}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{nodes}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
         \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{from\PYGZus{}layers}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{L}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{n}{layer}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{)}
         \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{compute}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{degree}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
         \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{execute}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{)}
    \PYG{p}{)}
    \PYG{n}{df} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{result}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{to\PYGZus{}pandas}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
    \PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+sa}{f}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n}{layer}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{: avg degree = }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n}{df}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{degree}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{mean}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{l+s+si}{:}\PYG{l+s+s2}{.2f}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\PYG{p}{)}

\subsection{How to Run Community Detection on Multilayer Networks}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/run_community_detection:how-to-run-community-detection-on-multilayer-networks}}\label{\detokenize{how-to/run_community_detection::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Goal:} This guide demonstrates how to apply community detection algorithms to multilayer networks and interpret their results. Community detection identifies \sphinxstyleemphasis{mesoscale structure}—groups of nodes that are more densely connected internally than to the rest of the network. In multilayer networks, communities can exist within single layers, span multiple layers, or emerge from inter\sphinxhyphen{}layer coupling patterns. This analysis is essential for understanding functional modules, organizational structure, and hierarchical clustering in complex systems.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Prerequisites:}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
A loaded multilayer network (see {\hyperref[\detokenize{how-to/load_and_build_networks::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{How to Load and Build Networks}}}})

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Basic familiarity with network terminology (nodes, edges, layers)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Understanding of modularity as a quality metric (covered in this guide)

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{When to use community detection:}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Identifying functional modules in biological networks

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Detecting organizational units in social networks

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Finding coherent topics in multi\sphinxhyphen{}relational knowledge graphs

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Analyzing temporal evolution of communities across time\sphinxhyphen{}sliced networks

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Discovering cross\sphinxhyphen{}layer relationships in multiplex systems

\end{itemize}


\subsubsection{Quick Start: Louvain Algorithm}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/run_community_detection:quick-start-louvain-algorithm}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{What is Louvain?}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The Louvain algorithm (Blondel et al., 2008) is a fast, greedy method that optimizes \sphinxstyleemphasis{modularity}, defined as:
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}Q = \frac{1}{2m} \sum_{ij} \left[ A_{ij} - \frac{k_i k_j}{2m} \right] \delta(c_i, c_j)\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
where \(A_{ij}\) is the adjacency matrix, \(k_i\) is node degree, \(m\) is total edges, and \(\delta(c_i, c_j)=1\) if nodes \(i,j\) are in the same community. Higher \(Q\) indicates stronger community structure.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{How it works:}
\begin{enumerate}
\sphinxsetlistlabels{\arabic}{enumi}{enumii}{}{.}%
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Initialize: each node starts in its own community

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
For each node, compute \(\Delta Q\) from moving to each neighbor’s community

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Move the node to the community with maximum positive \(\Delta Q\)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Aggregate: collapse communities into super\sphinxhyphen{}nodes and repeat

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Stop when no further improvement is possible

\end{enumerate}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Time complexity:} \(O(n \log n)\) for sparse networks

\sphinxAtStartPar

For layer\sphinxhyphen{}aware detection, use \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{louvain\_multilayer}} (see next section).


\subsubsection{Multilayer\sphinxhyphen{}Specific: Multilayer Louvain}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/run_community_detection:multilayer-specific-multilayer-louvain}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{What makes multilayer community detection different?}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Standard Louvain treats a multilayer network as a single flattened graph, losing layer identity. \sphinxstylestrong{Multilayer Louvain} (Mucha et al., 2010) optimizes the \sphinxstyleemphasis{multilayer modularity}:
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}Q_{\text{multi}} = \frac{1}{2\mu} \sum_{ij\alpha\beta} \left[ \left(A^\alpha_{ij} - \gamma^\alpha \frac{k_i^\alpha k_j^\alpha}{2m_\alpha}\right)\delta_{\alpha\beta} + \delta_{ij}\omega_{\alpha\beta} \right] \delta(g_{i\alpha}, g_{j\beta})\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
where:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(A^\alpha_{ij}\): adjacency in layer \(\alpha\)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(\gamma^\alpha\): resolution parameter for layer \(\alpha\) (default 1.0)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(\omega_{\alpha\beta}\): inter\sphinxhyphen{}layer coupling strength (default 1.0)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(\delta_{ij}=1\) if \(i=j\) (inter\sphinxhyphen{}layer edges connect same node across layers)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(\delta(g_{i\alpha}, g_{j\beta})=1\) if node \(i\) in layer \(\alpha\) and node \(j\) in layer \(\beta\) are in the same community

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(\mu\): total weight in supra\sphinxhyphen{}network

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Key insight:} The coupling term \(\omega_{\alpha\beta}\) controls whether communities span layers:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{ω = 0:} Layers are independent \(\rightarrow\) separate communities per layer

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{ω \(\rightarrow\) \(\infty\):} Strong coupling \(\rightarrow\) communities span all layers

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{0 \textless{} ω \textless{} \(\infty\):} Partial coupling \(\rightarrow\) communities can span some layers

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar

  Average community size: 30.0 node\PYGZhy{}layers
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Interpretation:}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{ω=0.0:} Each layer has independent communities (useful for baseline)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{ω=0.5\sphinxhyphen{}1.0:} Balanced trade\sphinxhyphen{}off, some communities span layers

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{ω\textgreater{}1.0:} Forces global communities across all layers (may over\sphinxhyphen{}integrate)

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Choosing ω:}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Use \sphinxstylestrong{domain knowledge}: biological function (high ω), temporal snapshots (low ω)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Grid search}: try ω ∈ {[}0.1, 0.5, 1.0, 2.0, 5.0{]} and pick maximum Q

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Consensus clustering}: aggregate results across multiple ω values

\end{itemize}


\subsubsection{Infomap Algorithm}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/run_community_detection:infomap-algorithm}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{What is Infomap?}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Infomap (Rosvall \& Bergstrom, 2008) uses information theory to find communities by minimizing the \sphinxstyleemphasis{map equation}:
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}L(M) = q_\curvearrowright H(Q) + \sum_{i=1}^m p_{\circlearrowright}^i H(P^i)\end{split}
\end{equation*}
\sphinxAtStartPar
where:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(q_\curvearrowright\): probability of switching between modules (inter\sphinxhyphen{}module flow)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(H(Q)\): entropy of module codebook

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(p_{\circlearrowright}^i\): probability of staying within module \(i\) (intra\sphinxhyphen{}module flow)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\(H(P^i)\): entropy of nodes within module \(i\)

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Key insight:} Infomap simulates a random walker and finds communities that compress the \sphinxstyleemphasis{description length} of the walker’s trajectory. Communities are regions where the walker gets “trapped” for extended periods.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Pros/cons vs. Louvain:}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Pros:} Often finds better communities for flow\sphinxhyphen{}based systems (e.g., citation networks, web graphs)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Cons:} Requires external binary (not pure Python), slower than Louvain, harder to interpret parameters

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Installation:}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Infomap requires the standalone binary from \sphinxurl{https://www.mapequation.org/infomap/}:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Download and install}
wget\PYG{+w}{ }https://www.mapequation.org/downloads/Infomap.zip
unzip\PYG{+w}{ }Infomap.zip
\PYG{n+nb}{cd}\PYG{+w}{ }Infomap
make
sudo\PYG{+w}{ }cp\PYG{+w}{ }Infomap\PYG{+w}{ }/usr/local/bin/infomap

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Or install Python wrapper (alternative)}
pip\PYG{+w}{ }install\PYG{+w}{ }infomap
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Basic usage:}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{py3plex}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{core}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{multinet}
\PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{py3plex}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{algorithms}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{community\PYGZus{}detection}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{community\PYGZus{}wrapper}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{infomap\PYGZus{}communities}
\PYG{k+kn}{import}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{os}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Load network}
\PYG{n}{network} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{multinet}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{multi\PYGZus{}layer\PYGZus{}network}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{directed}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{k+kc}{False}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{load\PYGZus{}network}\PYG{p}{(}
    \PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{datasets/synthetic\PYGZus{}multilayer.txt}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}
    \PYG{n}{input\PYGZus{}type}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{multiedgelist}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}
\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Check if binary exists}
\PYG{n}{binary\PYGZus{}path} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{/usr/local/bin/infomap}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}  \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Adjust to your installation}
\PYG{k}{if} \PYG{o+ow}{not} \PYG{n}{os}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{path}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{exists}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{binary\PYGZus{}path}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{:}
    \PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+sa}{f}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{Infomap binary not found at }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n}{binary\PYGZus{}path}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
    \PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{Please install from: https://www.mapequation.org/infomap/}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
    \PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{Falling back to Louvain...}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
    \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Use Louvain as fallback}
    \PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{py3plex}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{algorithms}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{community\PYGZus{}detection}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{community\PYGZus{}wrapper}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{louvain\PYGZus{}communities}
    \PYG{n}{communities} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{louvain\PYGZus{}communities}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{k}{else}\PYG{p}{:}
    \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Run Infomap}
    \PYG{n}{communities} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{infomap\PYGZus{}communities}\PYG{p}{(}
        \PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{,}
        \PYG{n}{binary}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{n}{binary\PYGZus{}path}\PYG{p}{,}
        \PYG{n}{multiplex}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{k+kc}{True}\PYG{p}{,}      \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Use multiplex mode for multilayer networks}
        \PYG{n}{iterations}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mi}{1000}\PYG{p}{,}     \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} More iterations = better convergence}
        \PYG{n}{seed}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mi}{42}\PYG{p}{,}             \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} For reproducibility}
        \PYG{n}{verbose}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{k+kc}{False}        \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Set True to see Infomap output}
    \PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Analyze results}
\PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{collections}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{Counter}
\PYG{n}{comm\PYGZus{}sizes} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{Counter}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{communities}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{values}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+sa}{f}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{Number of communities: }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n+nb}{len}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{comm\PYGZus{}sizes}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+sa}{f}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{Largest community: }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n+nb}{max}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{comm\PYGZus{}sizes}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{values}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{ nodes}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+sa}{f}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{Average size: }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n+nb}{sum}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{comm\PYGZus{}sizes}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{values}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{n+nb}{len}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{comm\PYGZus{}sizes}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{l+s+si}{:}\PYG{l+s+s2}{.1f}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Expected output:}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
Number of communities: 6
Largest community: 38 nodes
Average size: 20.0
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Multiplex mode:}

\sphinxAtStartPar
When \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{multiplex=True}}, Infomap treats layers as separate networks but allows random walkers to switch layers (implicitly modeling inter\sphinxhyphen{}layer coupling). This is different from Louvain’s explicit \(\omega\) parameter.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Comparison workflow:}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{sklearn}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{metrics}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{adjusted\PYGZus{}rand\PYGZus{}score}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{normalized\PYGZus{}mutual\PYGZus{}info\PYGZus{}score}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Run both algorithms}
\PYG{n}{louvain\PYGZus{}comms} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{louvain\PYGZus{}communities}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n}{infomap\PYGZus{}comms} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{infomap\PYGZus{}communities}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{binary}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{n}{binary\PYGZus{}path}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{seed}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mi}{42}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Convert to aligned label vectors}
\PYG{n}{nodes} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n+nb}{list}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{louvain\PYGZus{}comms}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{keys}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n}{louvain\PYGZus{}labels} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{p}{[}\PYG{n}{louvain\PYGZus{}comms}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{n}{n}\PYG{p}{]} \PYG{k}{for} \PYG{n}{n} \PYG{o+ow}{in} \PYG{n}{nodes}\PYG{p}{]}
\PYG{n}{infomap\PYGZus{}labels} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{p}{[}\PYG{n}{infomap\PYGZus{}comms}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{n}{n}\PYG{p}{]} \PYG{k}{for} \PYG{n}{n} \PYG{o+ow}{in} \PYG{n}{nodes}\PYG{p}{]}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Compute similarity}
\PYG{n}{ari} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{adjusted\PYGZus{}rand\PYGZus{}score}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{louvain\PYGZus{}labels}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{infomap\PYGZus{}labels}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n}{nmi} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{normalized\PYGZus{}mutual\PYGZus{}info\PYGZus{}score}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{louvain\PYGZus{}labels}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{infomap\PYGZus{}labels}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+sa}{f}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{Agreement between Louvain and Infomap:}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+sa}{f}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{  ARI: }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n}{ari}\PYG{l+s+si}{:}\PYG{l+s+s2}{.3f}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{  (1.0 = perfect agreement)}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+sa}{f}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{  NMI: }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n}{nmi}\PYG{l+s+si}{:}\PYG{l+s+s2}{.3f}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{  (1.0 = perfect agreement)}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Expected output:}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
Agreement between Louvain and Infomap:
  ARI: 0.723  (1.0 = perfect agreement)
  NMI: 0.815  (1.0 = perfect agreement)
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{When to use Infomap:}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Citation/web networks with clear flow patterns

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Networks where you care about information diffusion

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
When Louvain gives unsatisfying results (try both and compare)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
When you have the binary installed (otherwise, stick with Louvain)

\end{itemize}


\subsubsection{Label Propagation}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/run_community_detection:label-propagation}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{What is Label Propagation?}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Label propagation (Raghavan et al., 2007) is an extremely fast, near\sphinxhyphen{}linear time algorithm that works by iteratively assigning each node to the most common community among its neighbors.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Algorithm:}
\begin{enumerate}
\sphinxsetlistlabels{\arabic}{enumi}{enumii}{}{.}%
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Initialize: each node gets a unique label (community ID)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{For t=1 to T iterations:}
\begin{enumerate}
\sphinxsetlistlabels{\alph}{enumii}{enumiii}{}{.}%
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Randomize node order

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
For each node \(i\):
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Count neighbor labels: \(n_c = |\{j \in N(i) : c_j = c\}|\)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Assign \(c_i = \arg\max_c n_c\) (ties broken randomly)

\end{itemize}

\end{enumerate}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Stop when labels stabilize or max iterations reached

\end{enumerate}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Time complexity:} \(O(m)\) per iteration (linear in edges)

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Pros/cons:}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Pros:} Very fast, scales to millions of nodes, no parameters to tune

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Cons:} Non\sphinxhyphen{}deterministic (order\sphinxhyphen{}dependent), lower quality than Louvain/Infomap, may not converge

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Implementation note:}

\sphinxAtStartPar
py3plex uses NetworkX’s label propagation for single\sphinxhyphen{}layer networks:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{py3plex}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{core}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{multinet}
\PYG{k+kn}{import}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{networkx}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{as}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{nx}
\PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{networkx}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{algorithms}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{community}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{asyn\PYGZus{}lpa\PYGZus{}communities}
\PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{collections}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{defaultdict}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Load network}
\PYG{n}{network} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{multinet}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{multi\PYGZus{}layer\PYGZus{}network}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{directed}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{k+kc}{False}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{load\PYGZus{}network}\PYG{p}{(}
    \PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{datasets/synthetic\PYGZus{}multilayer.txt}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}
    \PYG{n}{input\PYGZus{}type}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{multiedgelist}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}
\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Convert to NetworkX (flattened single\PYGZhy{}layer graph)}
\PYG{n}{G} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{nx}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{Graph}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{k}{for} \PYG{n}{edge} \PYG{o+ow}{in} \PYG{n}{network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{core\PYGZus{}network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{edges}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{:}
    \PYG{n}{G}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{add\PYGZus{}edge}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{edge}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+m+mi}{0}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{edge}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Run label propagation}
\PYG{n}{communities\PYGZus{}list} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{asyn\PYGZus{}lpa\PYGZus{}communities}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{G}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{seed}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mi}{42}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Convert to dict format: node \PYGZhy{}\PYGZgt{} community\PYGZus{}id}
\PYG{n}{communities} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}
\PYG{k}{for} \PYG{n}{comm\PYGZus{}id}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{comm\PYGZus{}nodes} \PYG{o+ow}{in} \PYG{n+nb}{enumerate}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{communities\PYGZus{}list}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{:}
    \PYG{k}{for} \PYG{n}{node} \PYG{o+ow}{in} \PYG{n}{comm\PYGZus{}nodes}\PYG{p}{:}
        \PYG{n}{communities}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{n}{node}\PYG{p}{]} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{comm\PYGZus{}id}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Analyze results}
\PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{collections}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{Counter}
\PYG{n}{comm\PYGZus{}sizes} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{Counter}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{communities}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{values}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+sa}{f}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{Number of communities: }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n+nb}{len}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{comm\PYGZus{}sizes}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}

\subsubsection{Query Communities with DSL}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/run_community_detection:query-communities-with-dsl}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Goal:} Use py3plex’s Domain\sphinxhyphen{}Specific Language (DSL) to query and analyze community\sphinxhyphen{}detected networks efficiently.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The DSL provides a declarative, SQL\sphinxhyphen{}like interface for querying multilayer networks. After detecting communities, you can use DSL queries to filter nodes by community membership, compute community\sphinxhyphen{}level statistics, and extract subnetworks.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Prerequisites:}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Community detection results (e.g., from \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{louvain\_communities()}})

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Familiarity with DSL basics (see {\hyperref[\detokenize{how-to/query_with_dsl::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{How to Query Multilayer Graphs with the SQL\sphinxhyphen{}like DSL}}}} for full tutorial)

\end{itemize}


\paragraph{DSL Basics for Communities}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/run_community_detection:dsl-basics-for-communities}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{String Syntax \sphinxhyphen{} SQL\sphinxhyphen{}like queries:}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{py3plex}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{core}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{multinet}
\PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{py3plex}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{algorithms}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{community\PYGZus{}detection}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{community\PYGZus{}wrapper}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{louvain\PYGZus{}communities}
\PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{py3plex}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{dsl}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{execute\PYGZus{}query}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Load network and detect communities}
\PYG{n}{network} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{multinet}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{multi\PYGZus{}layer\PYGZus{}network}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{directed}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{k+kc}{False}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{load\PYGZus{}network}\PYG{p}{(}
    \PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{py3plex/datasets/\PYGZus{}data/synthetic\PYGZus{}multilayer.edges}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}
    \PYG{n}{input\PYGZus{}type}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{multiedgelist}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}
\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{n}{communities} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{louvain\PYGZus{}communities}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Attach community labels as node attributes}
\PYG{k}{for} \PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{node}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{layer}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{comm\PYGZus{}id} \PYG{o+ow}{in} \PYG{n}{communities}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{items}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{:}
    \PYG{n}{network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{core\PYGZus{}network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{nodes}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{node}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{layer}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{community}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{]} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{comm\PYGZus{}id}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} DSL Query: Find nodes in community 0}
\PYG{n}{result} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{execute\PYGZus{}query}\PYG{p}{(}
    \PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{,}
    \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{SELECT nodes WHERE community=0}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}
\PYG{p}{)}

\paragraph{Complex DSL Workflows}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/run_community_detection:complex-dsl-workflows}}

\sphinxstylestrong{Multi\sphinxhyphen{}step analysis: Find bridge nodes between communities:}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Bridge nodes: high betweenness + connect multiple communities}
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} First, compute betweenness}
\PYG{n}{result} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{p}{(}
    \PYG{n}{Q}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{nodes}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}

     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{execute}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Identify potential bridges (high betweenness)}

    \PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{node}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{data}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{betweenness\PYGZus{}centrality}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{)}
    \PYG{k}{for} \PYG{n}{node}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{data} \PYG{o+ow}{in} \PYG{n}{result}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{items}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
    \PYG{k}{if} \PYG{n}{data}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{betweenness\PYGZus{}centrality}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{]} \PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}} \PYG{l+m+mf}{0.01}  \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Threshold}
\PYG{p}{]}

\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+sa}{f}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{Potential bridge nodes (betweenness \PYGZgt{} 0.01): }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n+nb}{len}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{bridges}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}

    \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Get neighbors}

    \PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+sa}{f}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{  }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n}{node}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{: betweenness=}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n}{betw}\PYG{l+s+si}{:}\PYG{l+s+s2}{.6f}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{, connects }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n+nb}{len}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{neighbor\PYGZus{}comms}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{ communities}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}

\subsubsection{Compare Algorithms}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/run_community_detection:compare-algorithms}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Different algorithms optimize different objective functions and may produce different community structures. \sphinxstylestrong{Comparing multiple algorithms} helps validate findings and understand algorithm\sphinxhyphen{}specific biases.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Metrics for comparing partitions:}
\begin{enumerate}
\sphinxsetlistlabels{\arabic}{enumi}{enumii}{}{.}%
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Adjusted Rand Index (ARI)}: Measures similarity adjusted for chance
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Range: {[}\sphinxhyphen{}1, 1{]}, where 1 = perfect agreement, 0 = random

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Adjusted for cluster size imbalance

\end{itemize}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Normalized Mutual Information (NMI)}: Information\sphinxhyphen{}theoretic similarity
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Range: {[}0, 1{]}, where 1 = perfect agreement

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Symmetric, handles different number of communities well

\end{itemize}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Variation of Information (VI)}: Distance metric (lower = more similar)
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Range: {[}0, \(\infty\){]}, where 0 = identical partitions

\end{itemize}

\end{enumerate}

\PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{py3plex}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{algorithms}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{community\PYGZus{}detection}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{community\PYGZus{}wrapper}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{p}{(}

\item {}

\item {}

\end{itemize}

\subsubsection{Quality Metrics}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/run_community_detection:quality-metrics}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Why quality metrics matter:}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Quality metrics help you:
\begin{enumerate}
\sphinxsetlistlabels{\arabic}{enumi}{enumii}{}{.}%
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Compare algorithms} objectively

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Tune parameters} (e.g., choosing optimal \(\omega\) in multilayer Louvain)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Validate results} (high Q suggests real structure, not random fluctuations)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Detect overfitting} (too many tiny communities = over\sphinxhyphen{}segmentation)

\end{enumerate}


\paragraph{Compute Modularity}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/run_community_detection:compute-modularity}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Single\sphinxhyphen{}layer modularity:}

\sphinxAtStartPar
For flattened networks, use the Newman\sphinxhyphen{}Girvan modularity:
\begin{equation*}
\begin{split}Q = \frac{1}{2m} \sum_{ij} \left[ A_{ij} - \frac{k_i k_j}{2m} \right] \delta(c_i, c_j)\end{split}
\end{equation*}

\PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{py3plex}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{algorithms}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{community\PYGZus{}detection}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{community\PYGZus{}louvain}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{modularity}
\PYG{k+kn}{import}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{networkx}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{as}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{nx}

    \PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{datasets/synthetic\PYGZus{}multilayer.txt}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}
    \PYG{n}{input\PYGZus{}type}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{multiedgelist}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}
\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+sa}{f}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{Modularity Q: }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n}{Q}\PYG{l+s+si}{:}\PYG{l+s+s2}{.4f}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}

Modularity has a \sphinxstylestrong{resolution limit}: it cannot detect communities smaller than \(\sqrt{m}\) where \(m\) is the number of edges. The resolution parameter \(\gamma\) can help:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
