\subsection{How to Query Multilayer Graphs with the SQL\sphinxhyphen{}like DSL}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/query_with_dsl:how-to-query-multilayer-graphs-with-the-sql-like-dsl}}\label{\detokenize{how-to/query_with_dsl::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Goal:} Use py3plex’s SQL\sphinxhyphen{}inspired Domain\sphinxhyphen{}Specific Language (DSL) to query, filter, and analyze multilayer networks. The DSL is a \sphinxstylestrong{first\sphinxhyphen{}class query language} specifically designed for multilayer graph structures, providing both string syntax for interactive exploration and a type\sphinxhyphen{}safe builder API for production code.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{What Makes This DSL Special:}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Graph\sphinxhyphen{}aware}: Unlike generic query languages, the DSL understands multilayer structures—layers, layer intersections, intralayer vs. interlayer edges, and (node, layer) tuple semantics.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Dual interfaces}: String syntax for rapid prototyping in notebooks; builder API (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Q}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{L}}) for IDE autocompletion and type checking.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Integrated computation}: Compute centrality, clustering, and other network metrics directly in queries, with results returned as pandas DataFrames or NetworkX graphs.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Temporal support}: Query network snapshots and time ranges when your network includes temporal information.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Prerequisites:}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
A loaded \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{multi\_layer\_network}} object (see {\hyperref[\detokenize{how-to/load_and_build_networks::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{How to Load and Build Networks}}}})

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Basic familiarity with multilayer network concepts (nodes, layers, intralayer/interlayer edges)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
For complete DSL grammar and operator reference, see {\hyperref[\detokenize{reference/dsl_reference::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{DSL Reference}}}}

\end{itemize}


\subsubsection{Conceptual Overview}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/query_with_dsl:conceptual-overview}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The DSL has \sphinxstylestrong{two complementary interfaces} that compile to the same internal representation:
\begin{enumerate}
\sphinxsetlistlabels{\arabic}{enumi}{enumii}{}{.}%
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{String Syntax} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{execute\_query(network, "SELECT nodes WHERE ...")}})
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
SQL\sphinxhyphen{}like, human\sphinxhyphen{}readable

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Ideal for interactive exploration in Jupyter notebooks or the REPL

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Quick one\sphinxhyphen{}liners for common queries

\end{itemize}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Builder API} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Q.nodes().where(...).compute(...).execute(network)}})
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Pythonic, chainable methods

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Type\sphinxhyphen{}safe with IDE autocompletion

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Recommended for production code and complex workflows

\end{itemize}

\end{enumerate}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Mental Model:}

\sphinxAtStartPar
A typical DSL query follows this pipeline:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
SELECT nodes/edges
\(\rightarrow\) FROM LAYERS (restrict to specific layers)
\(\rightarrow\) WHERE (filter by attributes or special predicates)
\(\rightarrow\) COMPUTE (calculate metrics like degree, centrality)
\(\rightarrow\) ORDER BY (sort results)
\(\rightarrow\) LIMIT (cap number of results)
\(\rightarrow\) EXPORT (materialize as DataFrame, NetworkX graph, etc.)
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Key Concepts:}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Nodes as (node, layer) tuples}: In multilayer networks, a node may appear in multiple layers. The DSL represents these as \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{(node\_id, layer\_name)}} pairs.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Layer algebra}: Combine layers with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{+}} (union), \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\&}} (intersection), or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\sphinxhyphen{}}} (difference).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Special predicates}: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{intralayer=True}} selects edges within a layer; \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{interlayer=("layer1", "layer2")}} selects edges crossing specific layers.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Lazy execution}: Queries are built incrementally and executed only when \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.execute(network)}} is called.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Comparison to SQL:}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Think of the DSL as SQL for graphs:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{SELECT nodes WHERE degree \textgreater{} 5}} ≈ SQL’s \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{SELECT * FROM nodes WHERE degree \textgreater{} 5}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
But instead of tables, you’re querying \sphinxstylestrong{nodes and edges} with \sphinxstylestrong{multilayer and temporal attributes}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Layer filters and graph\sphinxhyphen{}specific predicates (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{intralayer}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{interlayer}}) have no SQL equivalent

\end{itemize}


\subsubsection{String Syntax (Quick and Readable)}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/query_with_dsl:string-syntax-quick-and-readable}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The string syntax provides a concise, SQL\sphinxhyphen{}like way to express queries. Best for exploratory analysis and quick investigations.


\paragraph{Basic SELECT}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/query_with_dsl:basic-select}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Select all nodes and inspect the result:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{py3plex}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{core}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{multinet}
\PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{py3plex}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{dsl}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{execute\PYGZus{}query}

\PYG{n}{network} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{multinet}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{multi\PYGZus{}layer\PYGZus{}network}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{load\PYGZus{}network}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{data.multiedgelist}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{input\PYGZus{}type}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{multiedgelist}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Get all nodes}
\PYG{n}{result} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{execute\PYGZus{}query}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{SELECT nodes}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+sa}{f}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{Found }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n+nb}{len}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{result}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{ nodes}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Inspect a few items}
\PYG{k}{for} \PYG{n}{i}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{node}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{data}\PYG{p}{)} \PYG{o+ow}{in} \PYG{n+nb}{enumerate}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{result}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{items}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{:}
    \PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+sa}{f}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{  }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n}{node}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{: }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n}{data}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
    \PYG{k}{if} \PYG{n}{i} \PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}}\PYG{o}{=} \PYG{l+m+mi}{4}\PYG{p}{:}
        \PYG{k}{break}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Expected output:}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
Found 100 nodes
  (\PYGZsq{}alice\PYGZsq{}, \PYGZsq{}social\PYGZsq{}): \PYGZob{}\PYGZsq{}degree\PYGZsq{}: 7, \PYGZsq{}layer\PYGZsq{}: \PYGZsq{}social\PYGZsq{}, \PYGZsq{}layer\PYGZus{}count\PYGZsq{}: 2\PYGZcb{}
  (\PYGZsq{}bob\PYGZsq{}, \PYGZsq{}social\PYGZsq{}): \PYGZob{}\PYGZsq{}degree\PYGZsq{}: 5, \PYGZsq{}layer\PYGZsq{}: \PYGZsq{}social\PYGZsq{}, \PYGZsq{}layer\PYGZus{}count\PYGZsq{}: 1\PYGZcb{}
  (\PYGZsq{}charlie\PYGZsq{}, \PYGZsq{}work\PYGZsq{}): \PYGZob{}\PYGZsq{}degree\PYGZsq{}: 3, \PYGZsq{}layer\PYGZsq{}: \PYGZsq{}work\PYGZsq{}, \PYGZsq{}layer\PYGZus{}count\PYGZsq{}: 2\PYGZcb{}
  (\PYGZsq{}diana\PYGZsq{}, \PYGZsq{}social\PYGZsq{}): \PYGZob{}\PYGZsq{}degree\PYGZsq{}: 9, \PYGZsq{}layer\PYGZsq{}: \PYGZsq{}social\PYGZsq{}, \PYGZsq{}layer\PYGZus{}count\PYGZsq{}: 3\PYGZcb{}
  (\PYGZsq{}eve\PYGZsq{}, \PYGZsq{}work\PYGZsq{}): \PYGZob{}\PYGZsq{}degree\PYGZsq{}: 4, \PYGZsq{}layer\PYGZsq{}: \PYGZsq{}work\PYGZsq{}, \PYGZsq{}layer\PYGZus{}count\PYGZsq{}: 1\PYGZcb{}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Note:} Keys are \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{(node, layer)}} tuples representing node\sphinxhyphen{}layer pairs. The \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{layer\_count}} attribute indicates how many layers the node appears in across the entire network.


\paragraph{Filter by Layer}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/query_with_dsl:filter-by-layer}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Restrict queries to nodes in a specific layer:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Get nodes in the \PYGZsq{}friends\PYGZsq{} layer only}
\PYG{n}{result} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{execute\PYGZus{}query}\PYG{p}{(}
    \PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{,}
    \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{SELECT nodes WHERE layer=}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{friends}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}
\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+sa}{f}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{Nodes in }\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{friends}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{ layer: }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n+nb}{len}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{result}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Understanding Layer Filters:}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{layer="friends"}} selects only the node\sphinxhyphen{}layer pairs where \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{layer == "friends"}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
This does \sphinxstylestrong{not} select all occurrences of nodes across layers—only their representation in the specified layer

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Use \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{layer\_count \textgreater{}= 2}} to find nodes appearing in multiple layers

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Example with statistics:}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{result} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{execute\PYGZus{}query}\PYG{p}{(}
    \PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{,}
    \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{SELECT nodes WHERE layer=}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{friends}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{ COMPUTE degree}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}
\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n}{df} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{result}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{to\PYGZus{}pandas}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+sa}{f}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{Nodes in }\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{friends}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{: }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n+nb}{len}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{df}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+sa}{f}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{Average degree in }\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{friends}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{: }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n}{df}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{degree}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{mean}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{l+s+si}{:}\PYG{l+s+s2}{.2f}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+sa}{f}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{Max degree in }\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{friends}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{: }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n}{df}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{degree}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{max}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Expected output:}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
Nodes in \PYGZsq{}friends\PYGZsq{}: 42
Average degree in \PYGZsq{}friends\PYGZsq{}: 5.23
Max degree in \PYGZsq{}friends\PYGZsq{}: 15
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\paragraph{Filter by Property}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/query_with_dsl:filter-by-property}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Use comparisons to filter nodes by computed or intrinsic attributes:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} High\PYGZhy{}degree nodes}
\PYG{n}{result} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{execute\PYGZus{}query}\PYG{p}{(}
    \PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{,}
    \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{SELECT nodes WHERE degree \PYGZgt{} 5}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}
\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+sa}{f}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{High\PYGZhy{}degree nodes: }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n+nb}{len}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{result}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Multilayer nodes with high degree}
\PYG{n}{result} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{execute\PYGZus{}query}\PYG{p}{(}
    \PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{,}
    \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{SELECT nodes WHERE degree \PYGZgt{} 5 AND layer\PYGZus{}count \PYGZgt{}= 2}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}
\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+sa}{f}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{High\PYGZhy{}degree multilayer nodes: }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n+nb}{len}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{result}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Supported operators:} \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\textgreater{}}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\textgreater{}=}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\textless{}}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\textless{}=}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{=}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{!=}}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Multiple conditions} are combined with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{AND}}. For more complex logic, use the builder API (see below).

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Expected output:}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
High\PYGZhy{}degree nodes: 34
High\PYGZhy{}degree multilayer nodes: 18
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\paragraph{Compute Statistics}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/query_with_dsl:compute-statistics}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{COMPUTE}} clause calculates network metrics and attaches them to result rows. This is where the DSL becomes powerful for analysis:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Compute degree and betweenness centrality for nodes in \PYGZsq{}social\PYGZsq{} layer}
\PYG{n}{result} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{execute\PYGZus{}query}\PYG{p}{(}
    \PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{,}
    \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{SELECT nodes WHERE layer=}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{social}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{ }\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}
    \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{COMPUTE degree COMPUTE betweenness\PYGZus{}centrality}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}
\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Convert to pandas for analysis}
\PYG{n}{df} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{result}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{to\PYGZus{}pandas}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{Top nodes by betweenness centrality:}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{df}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{id}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{degree}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{betweenness\PYGZus{}centrality}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{head}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+se}{\PYGZbs{}n}\PYG{l+s+s2}{Summary statistics:}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{df}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{degree}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{betweenness\PYGZus{}centrality}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{describe}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Expected output:}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
Top nodes by betweenness centrality:
                 id  degree  betweenness\PYGZus{}centrality
0  (alice, social)      12                 0.245
1    (bob, social)       8                 0.189
2    (eve, social)      15                 0.301
3  (frank, social)       7                 0.134
4  (grace, social)      11                 0.221

Summary statistics:
             degree  betweenness\PYGZus{}centrality
count     65.000000               65.000000
mean       6.846154                0.112308
std        3.241057                0.089542
min        1.000000                0.000000
25\PYGZpc{}        4.000000                0.045000
50\PYGZpc{}        7.000000                0.089000
75\PYGZpc{}       10.000000                0.167000
max       15.000000                0.301000
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Available measures} include: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{degree}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{betweenness\_centrality}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{closeness\_centrality}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{eigenvector\_centrality}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pagerank}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{clustering}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{communities}}. See {\hyperref[\detokenize{reference/dsl_reference::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{DSL Reference}}}} for the complete list.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Use case:} This pattern is ideal for generating summary statistics for papers, reports, or further statistical analysis.


\subsubsection{Builder API (Type\sphinxhyphen{}Safe)}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/query_with_dsl:builder-api-type-safe}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The \sphinxstylestrong{builder API is the recommended approach for production code}. It provides:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
IDE autocompletion and inline documentation

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Type checking with tools like mypy

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Clearer error messages

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Easier refactoring and composition of queries

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
All builder queries compile to the same AST as string queries, ensuring consistent semantics.


\paragraph{Basic Queries}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/query_with_dsl:basic-queries}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Create and execute queries using the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Q}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{L}} imports:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{py3plex}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{dsl}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{Q}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{L}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Get all nodes}
\PYG{n}{result} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{Q}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{nodes}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{execute}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+sa}{f}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{Total nodes: }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n+nb}{len}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{result}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Get nodes from a specific layer}
\PYG{n}{result} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{p}{(}
    \PYG{n}{Q}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{nodes}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{from\PYGZus{}layers}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{L}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{friends}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{)}
     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{execute}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+sa}{f}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{Nodes in }\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{friends}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{ layer: }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n+nb}{len}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{result}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Query reusability:} You can define a query once and execute it with different networks:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{high\PYGZus{}degree\PYGZus{}query} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{Q}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{nodes}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{where}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{degree\PYGZus{}\PYGZus{}gt}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mi}{10}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{compute}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{betweenness\PYGZus{}centrality}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Execute on multiple networks}
\PYG{n}{result\PYGZus{}network1} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{high\PYGZus{}degree\PYGZus{}query}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{execute}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network1}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n}{result\PYGZus{}network2} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{high\PYGZus{}degree\PYGZus{}query}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{execute}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network2}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\paragraph{Filtering}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/query_with_dsl:filtering}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Use \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{where()}} to add filter conditions. The builder API uses Django\sphinxhyphen{}style \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\_\_}} suffixes for comparisons:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Filter by property}
\PYG{n}{result} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{p}{(}
    \PYG{n}{Q}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{nodes}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{where}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{degree\PYGZus{}\PYGZus{}gt}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mi}{5}\PYG{p}{)}
     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{execute}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+sa}{f}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{Nodes with degree \PYGZgt{} 5: }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n+nb}{len}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{result}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Multiple conditions (combined with AND)}
\PYG{n}{result} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{p}{(}
    \PYG{n}{Q}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{nodes}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{from\PYGZus{}layers}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{L}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{work}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{)}
     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{where}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{degree\PYGZus{}\PYGZus{}gt}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mi}{3}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{layer\PYGZus{}count\PYGZus{}\PYGZus{}gte}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mi}{2}\PYG{p}{)}
     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{execute}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+sa}{f}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{Multilayer high\PYGZhy{}degree nodes in }\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{work}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{: }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n+nb}{len}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{result}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Supported comparison suffixes:}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\_\_gt}}: greater than (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\textgreater{}}})

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\_\_gte}} or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\_\_ge}}: greater than or equal (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\textgreater{}=}})

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\_\_lt}}: less than (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\textless{}}})

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\_\_lte}} or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\_\_le}}: less than or equal (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\textless{}=}})

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\_\_eq}}: equal (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{=}})

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\_\_ne}} or \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\_\_neq}}: not equal (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{!=}})

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Understanding} \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{layer\_count}}:

\sphinxAtStartPar
In multilayer networks, a node may appear in multiple layers. The \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{layer\_count}} attribute indicates how many layers the node participates in:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{layer\_count\_\_gte=2}}: nodes appearing in at least 2 layers

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{layer\_count\_\_eq=1}}: nodes appearing in exactly 1 layer (layer\sphinxhyphen{}specific nodes)

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
This is useful for identifying “connector” nodes that bridge multiple contexts.


\paragraph{Computing Metrics}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/query_with_dsl:computing-metrics}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Use \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{compute()}} to calculate network metrics. Metrics are computed efficiently and attached to result rows:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Compute multiple metrics}
\PYG{n}{result} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{p}{(}
    \PYG{n}{Q}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{nodes}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{compute}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{degree}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{betweenness\PYGZus{}centrality}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{clustering}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{execute}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Convert to DataFrame and analyze}
\PYG{n}{df} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{result}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{to\PYGZus{}pandas}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{df}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{head}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mi}{10}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Get top nodes by a metric}
\PYG{n}{top\PYGZus{}by\PYGZus{}betweenness} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{df}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{nlargest}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mi}{10}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{betweenness\PYGZus{}centrality}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+se}{\PYGZbs{}n}\PYG{l+s+s2}{Top 10 nodes by betweenness centrality:}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{top\PYGZus{}by\PYGZus{}betweenness}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{id}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{betweenness\PYGZus{}centrality}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{degree}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Order of operations:}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{compute()}} can be called at any point in the chain

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Filters (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{where()}}) can reference computed metrics only if the metric is computed \sphinxstylestrong{before} the filter

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
For best performance, filter first, then compute:

\end{itemize}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Good: Filter first, then compute}
\PYG{n}{result} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{p}{(}
    \PYG{n}{Q}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{nodes}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{from\PYGZus{}layers}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{L}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{social}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{)}
     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{where}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{degree\PYGZus{}\PYGZus{}gt}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mi}{5}\PYG{p}{)}

\paragraph{Sorting and Limiting}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/query_with_dsl:sorting-and-limiting}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Use \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{order\_by()}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{limit()}} to control result ordering and size:

\PYG{n}{result} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{p}{(}
    \PYG{n}{Q}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{nodes}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{compute}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{degree}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{order\PYGZus{}by}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZhy{}degree}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}  \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} \PYGZdq{}\PYGZhy{}\PYGZdq{} prefix for descending}
     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{limit}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mi}{10}\PYG{p}{)}
     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{execute}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{Top 10 highest\PYGZhy{}degree nodes:}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{k}{for} \PYG{n}{node}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{data} \PYG{o+ow}{in} \PYG{n}{result}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{items}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{:}
    \PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+sa}{f}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{  }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n}{node}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{: degree=}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n}{data}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{degree}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}

\subsubsection{Working with Results}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/query_with_dsl:working-with-results}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
DSL queries return a \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{QueryResult}} object that provides multiple ways to access and export data. Understanding how to work with results is crucial for integrating DSL queries into analysis pipelines.

\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+sa}{f}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{Sample value: }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n}{sample\PYGZus{}value}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{n}{df} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{result}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{to\PYGZus{}pandas}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Use pandas boolean indexing}
\PYG{n}{filtered} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{df}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{n}{df}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{degree}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{]} \PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}} \PYG{l+m+mi}{5}\PYG{p}{]}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Complex conditions}
\PYG{n}{interesting\PYGZus{}nodes} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{df}\PYG{p}{[}
    \PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{df}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{degree}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{]} \PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}} \PYG{l+m+mi}{5}\PYG{p}{)} \PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}}
    \PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{df}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{betweenness\PYGZus{}centrality}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{]} \PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}} \PYG{n}{df}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{betweenness\PYGZus{}centrality}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{mean}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{p}{]}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Performance note:} For very large networks (millions of nodes), filtering in the DSL query (Option 1) is most efficient because it avoids materializing unnecessary results. For smaller networks, pandas filtering (Option 3) is often more convenient.


\subsubsection{Advanced Queries}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/query_with_dsl:advanced-queries}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This section showcases the DSL’s power for sophisticated multilayer network analysis. These patterns are common in research and can be adapted to your specific needs.


\paragraph{Multiple Layer Selection}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/query_with_dsl:multiple-layer-selection}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Use \sphinxstylestrong{layer algebra} to combine layers. The \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{L}} object supports set operations:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{py3plex}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{dsl}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{Q}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{L}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Union: nodes/edges from EITHER layer}
\PYG{n}{result} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{p}{(}
    \PYG{n}{Q}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{nodes}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{from\PYGZus{}layers}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{L}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{friends}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{]} \PYG{o}{+} \PYG{n}{L}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{work}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{)}
     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{compute}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{degree}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{execute}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{n}{df} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{result}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{to\PYGZus{}pandas}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+sa}{f}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{Combined nodes from }\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{friends}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{ and }\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{work}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{: }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n+nb}{len}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{df}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+sa}{f}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{Average degree across both layers: }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n}{df}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{degree}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{mean}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{l+s+si}{:}\PYG{l+s+s2}{.2f}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Set semantics:}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{L{[}"friends"{]} + L{[}"work"{]}}}: \sphinxstylestrong{Union} of nodes/edges from both layers (nodes appearing in either layer)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{L{[}"friends"{]} \& L{[}"work"{]}}}: \sphinxstylestrong{Intersection} (see next section)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{L{[}"friends"{]} \sphinxhyphen{} L{[}"work"{]}}}: \sphinxstylestrong{Difference} (nodes in friends but not work)

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Use case:} Compare activity across related contexts. For example, analyze user behavior across social and professional networks together.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Expected output:}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
Combined nodes from \PYGZsq{}friends\PYGZsq{} and \PYGZsq{}work\PYGZsq{}: 87
Average degree across both layers: 6.12
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\paragraph{Layer Intersection}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/query_with_dsl:layer-intersection}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Find nodes that appear in \sphinxstylestrong{multiple specific layers}:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Nodes present in BOTH \PYGZsq{}friends\PYGZsq{} AND \PYGZsq{}work\PYGZsq{} layers}
\PYG{n}{result} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{p}{(}
    \PYG{n}{Q}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{nodes}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{from\PYGZus{}layers}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{L}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{friends}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{]} \PYG{o}{\PYGZam{}} \PYG{n}{L}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{work}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{)}
     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{compute}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{degree}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{betweenness\PYGZus{}centrality}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{execute}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{n}{df} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{result}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{to\PYGZus{}pandas}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+sa}{f}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{Nodes in both }\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{friends}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{ and }\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{work}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{: }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n+nb}{len}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{df}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+se}{\PYGZbs{}n}\PYG{l+s+s2}{These are }\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{connector}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{ nodes bridging social and professional contexts}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{df}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{head}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mi}{10}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Semantics:}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{L{[}"friends"{]} \& L{[}"work"{]}}} selects nodes that have representations in \sphinxstylestrong{both} layers

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
This is different from \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{layer\_count \textgreater{}= 2}}, which selects nodes in \sphinxstylestrong{any} two layers

\item {}

\PYG{p}{)}

\paragraph{Query Edges}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/query_with_dsl:query-edges}}

The DSL supports edge queries with the same flexibility as node queries:

     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{execute}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{n}{df} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{edges}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{to\PYGZus{}pandas}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+se}{\PYGZbs{}n}\PYG{l+s+s2}{Sample edges:}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{df}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{head}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Analyze edge distribution}
\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+sa}{f}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+se}{\PYGZbs{}n}\PYG{l+s+s2}{Mean edge weight: }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n}{df}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{weight}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{mean}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{l+s+si}{:}\PYG{l+s+s2}{.3f}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+sa}{f}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{Mean edge betweenness: }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n}{df}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{edge\PYGZus{}betweenness}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{mean}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{l+s+si}{:}\PYG{l+s+s2}{.3f}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}

\subsubsection{Temporal Queries}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/query_with_dsl:temporal-queries}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The DSL supports temporal filtering for networks with time\sphinxhyphen{}stamped edges or nodes. Use \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.at(t)}} for point\sphinxhyphen{}in\sphinxhyphen{}time snapshots and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.during(t0, t1)}} for time ranges.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Prerequisites for temporal queries:}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Edges or nodes must have temporal attributes:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Point\sphinxhyphen{}in\sphinxhyphen{}time}: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{t}} attribute (e.g., \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\{"t": 150.0\}}})

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Intervals}: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{t\_start}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{t\_end}} attributes (e.g., \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\{"t\_start": 100.0, "t\_end": 200.0\}}})

\end{itemize}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Time values are typically numeric (timestamps) or ISO date strings

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Temporal semantics:}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{at(t)}}: Selects entities active at a specific moment
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
For point\sphinxhyphen{}in\sphinxhyphen{}time edges: includes edges where \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{t\_edge == t}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
For interval edges: includes edges where \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{t}} is in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{{[}t\_start, t\_end{]}}}

\end{itemize}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{during(t0, t1)}}: Selects entities active during a time window
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
For point\sphinxhyphen{}in\sphinxhyphen{}time edges: includes edges where \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{t}} is in \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{{[}t0, t1{]}}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
For interval edges: includes edges where the interval \sphinxstylestrong{overlaps} \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{{[}t0, t1{]}}}

\end{itemize}

\end{itemize}


\paragraph{Filter by Time (Snapshot)}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/query_with_dsl:filter-by-time-snapshot}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Query the network state at a specific point in time:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Nodes active at t=150.0}
\PYG{n}{result} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{p}{(}
    \PYG{n}{Q}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{nodes}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{at}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mf}{150.0}\PYG{p}{)}
     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{compute}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{degree}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{execute}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{n}{df} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{result}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{to\PYGZus{}pandas}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+sa}{f}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{Nodes active at t=150: }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n+nb}{len}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{df}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+sa}{f}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{Average degree at t=150: }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n}{df}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{degree}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{mean}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{l+s+si}{:}\PYG{l+s+s2}{.2f}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+se}{\PYGZbs{}n}\PYG{l+s+s2}{Top nodes by degree at this snapshot:}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{df}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{nlargest}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mi}{5}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{degree}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{id}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{degree}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\paragraph{Time Range}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/query_with_dsl:time-range}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Query entities active during a time window:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Nodes active during January 2024 (assuming numeric timestamps)}
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} For ISO dates, use strings: .during(\PYGZdq{}2024\PYGZhy{}01\PYGZhy{}01\PYGZdq{}, \PYGZdq{}2024\PYGZhy{}01\PYGZhy{}31\PYGZdq{})}
\PYG{n}{result} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{p}{(}
    \PYG{n}{Q}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{nodes}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{during}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mf}{100.0}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mf}{200.0}\PYG{p}{)}
     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{compute}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{degree}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{execute}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{n}{df} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{result}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{to\PYGZus{}pandas}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+sa}{f}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{Nodes active during [100, 200]: }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n+nb}{len}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{df}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Compare to snapshot}
\PYG{n}{snapshot\PYGZus{}result} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{Q}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{nodes}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{at}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mf}{150.0}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{execute}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+sa}{f}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{Nodes at t=150 (snapshot): }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n+nb}{len}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{snapshot\PYGZus{}result}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+sa}{f}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{Nodes during [100, 200] (range): }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n+nb}{len}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{df}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+sa}{f}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{Ratio: }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n+nb}{len}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{df}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{/}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nb}{len}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{snapshot\PYGZus{}result}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{l+s+si}{:}\PYG{l+s+s2}{.2f}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{x more nodes in range}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Open\sphinxhyphen{}ended ranges:}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} From t=100 onwards (no upper limit)}
\PYG{n}{result\PYGZus{}after} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{Q}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{edges}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{during}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mf}{100.0}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{k+kc}{None}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{execute}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Up to t=200 (no lower limit)}
\PYG{n}{result\PYGZus{}before} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{Q}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{edges}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{during}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{k+kc}{None}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mf}{200.0}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{execute}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Use case:} Study network evolution, identify persistent vs. transient connections, analyze activity bursts.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Expected output:}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]

Nodes at t=150 (snapshot): 78

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Temporal edges example:}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Edges active during a period}
\PYG{n}{edges} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{p}{(}
    \PYG{n}{Q}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{edges}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{during}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mf}{100.0}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mf}{200.0}\PYG{p}{)}
     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{compute}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{edge\PYGZus{}betweenness}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{execute}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{n}{df} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{edges}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{to\PYGZus{}pandas}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+sa}{f}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{Active edges during [100, 200]: }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n+nb}{len}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{df}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+sa}{f}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{Mean edge betweenness: }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n}{df}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{edge\PYGZus{}betweenness}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{mean}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{l+s+si}{:}\PYG{l+s+s2}{.4f}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Note on implementation status:}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Temporal queries are \sphinxstylestrong{fully implemented} for edge\sphinxhyphen{}level temporal data. Node\sphinxhyphen{}level temporal filtering depends on your network’s representation:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
If nodes have explicit \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{t}} attributes, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.at()}} and \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.during()}} work directly

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
If only edges are timestamped, node activity is inferred from edge presence

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
For most use cases, temporal edge queries are sufficient

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
See {\hyperref[\detokenize{reference/dsl_reference::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{DSL Reference}}}} for complete temporal query syntax and examples with ISO date strings.


\subsubsection{Common Patterns}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/query_with_dsl:common-patterns}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This section presents \sphinxstylestrong{end\sphinxhyphen{}to\sphinxhyphen{}end recipes} for common multilayer network analysis tasks. These patterns are production\sphinxhyphen{}ready and can be adapted to your research questions.


\paragraph{Pattern: Find Influential Nodes}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/query_with_dsl:pattern-find-influential-nodes}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Identify nodes that are both well\sphinxhyphen{}connected (high degree) and structurally important (high betweenness centrality):

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} High\PYGZhy{}degree nodes ranked by betweenness centrality}
\PYG{n}{result} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{p}{(}
    \PYG{n}{Q}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{nodes}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{compute}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{degree}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{betweenness\PYGZus{}centrality}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{layer\PYGZus{}count}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{where}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{degree\PYGZus{}\PYGZus{}gt}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mi}{10}\PYG{p}{)}
     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{order\PYGZus{}by}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZhy{}betweenness\PYGZus{}centrality}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{limit}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mi}{20}\PYG{p}{)}
     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{execute}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{n}{df} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{result}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{to\PYGZus{}pandas}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+sa}{f}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{Top 20 influential nodes (degree \PYGZgt{} 10):}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{df}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{id}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{degree}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{betweenness\PYGZus{}centrality}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{layer\PYGZus{}count}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Export for further analysis or publication}
\PYG{n}{df}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{to\PYGZus{}csv}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{influential\PYGZus{}nodes.csv}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{index}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{k+kc}{False}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Visualize}
\PYG{k+kn}{import}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{matplotlib}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{pyplot}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{as}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{plt}
\PYG{n}{plt}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{figure}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{figsize}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mi}{10}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mi}{6}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n}{plt}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{scatter}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{df}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{degree}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{df}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{betweenness\PYGZus{}centrality}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{,}
            \PYG{n}{s}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{n}{df}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{layer\PYGZus{}count}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{l+m+mi}{50}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{alpha}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mf}{0.6}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n}{plt}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{xlabel}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{Degree}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n}{plt}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{ylabel}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{Betweenness Centrality}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n}{plt}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{title}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{Influential Nodes (size = layer\PYGZus{}count)}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n}{plt}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{tight\PYGZus{}layout}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n}{plt}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{savefig}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{influential\PYGZus{}nodes.png}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{dpi}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mi}{300}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Why this pattern works:}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Degree} measures local connectivity (how many neighbors)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Betweenness centrality} measures global importance (how often the node appears on shortest paths)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Nodes high in both metrics are \sphinxstylestrong{influential bridges} in the network

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Expected output:}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
Top 20 influential nodes (degree \PYGZgt{} 10):
                   id  degree  betweenness\PYGZus{}centrality  layer\PYGZus{}count
0     (eve, social)      15                 0.301000            3
1   (alice, social)      12                 0.245000            2
2   (grace, social)      11                 0.221000            2
3     (bob, social)      12                 0.198000            1
4   (diana, work)        14                 0.187000            3
...
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\paragraph{Pattern: Compare Layer Activity}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/query_with_dsl:pattern-compare-layer-activity}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Compute summary statistics for each layer to understand layer\sphinxhyphen{}specific dynamics:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{layers} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{get\PYGZus{}layers}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{n}{layer\PYGZus{}stats} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{p}{[}\PYG{p}{]}
\PYG{k}{for} \PYG{n}{layer} \PYG{o+ow}{in} \PYG{n}{layers}\PYG{p}{:}
    \PYG{n}{result} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{p}{(}
        \PYG{n}{Q}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{nodes}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
         \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{from\PYGZus{}layers}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{L}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{n}{layer}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{)}
         \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{compute}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{degree}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{clustering}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
         \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{execute}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{)}
    \PYG{p}{)}
    \PYG{n}{df} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{result}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{to\PYGZus{}pandas}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}

    \PYG{n}{layer\PYGZus{}stats}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{append}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}
        \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{layer}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{n}{layer}\PYG{p}{,}
        \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{num\PYGZus{}nodes}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{n+nb}{len}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{df}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{,}
        \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{mean\PYGZus{}degree}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{n}{df}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{degree}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{mean}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{,}
        \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{max\PYGZus{}degree}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{n}{df}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{degree}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{max}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{,}
        \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{mean\PYGZus{}clustering}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{n}{df}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{clustering}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{mean}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{,}
    \PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{)}

    \PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+sa}{f}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n}{layer}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{: }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n+nb}{len}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{df}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{ nodes, }\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}
          \PYG{l+s+sa}{f}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{avg degree=}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n}{df}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{degree}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{mean}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{l+s+si}{:}\PYG{l+s+s2}{.2f}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{, }\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}
          \PYG{l+s+sa}{f}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{avg clustering=}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n}{df}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{clustering}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{mean}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{l+s+si}{:}\PYG{l+s+s2}{.3f}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}

\paragraph{Pattern: Export Subnetwork}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Extract a subnetwork based on query criteria for focused analysis or visualization:

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Extract high\PYGZhy{}activity multilayer nodes}
\PYG{n}{active\PYGZus{}nodes} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{p}{(}
    \PYG{n}{Q}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{nodes}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{where}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{layer\PYGZus{}count\PYGZus{}\PYGZus{}gt}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mi}{2}\PYG{p}{)}
     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{compute}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{degree}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{betweenness\PYGZus{}centrality}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{execute}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+sa}{f}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{Selected }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n+nb}{len}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{active\PYGZus{}nodes}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{ multilayer nodes}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+sa}{f}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{Subnetwork: }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n}{subnetwork}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{number\PYGZus{}of\PYGZus{}nodes}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{ nodes, }\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}
      \PYG{l+s+sa}{f}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n}{subnetwork}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{number\PYGZus{}of\PYGZus{}edges}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{ edges}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+sa}{f}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+se}{\PYGZbs{}n}\PYG{l+s+s2}{Subnetwork mean degree: }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n}{df}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{degree}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{mean}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{l+s+si}{:}\PYG{l+s+s2}{.2f}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+sa}{f}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{Subnetwork mean betweenness: }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n}{df}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{betweenness\PYGZus{}centrality}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{mean}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{l+s+si}{:}\PYG{l+s+s2}{.4f}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{n}{plt}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{savefig}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{subnetwork\PYGZus{}viz.png}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{dpi}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mi}{300}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{execute}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{execute}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{)}

This pattern is often combined with community detection, dynamics simulation, or centrality analysis:

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} 1. Select subnetwork}

\PYG{n}{subnetwork} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{subgraph}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{core\PYGZus{}nodes}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{keys}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{n}{communities} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{louvain\PYGZus{}communities}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{subnetwork}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} 3. Analyze communities}
\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+sa}{f}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{Found }\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{n+nb}{len}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n+nb}{set}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{communities}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{values}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{l+s+si}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{ communities}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} 4. Visualize or export}
\PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{py3plex}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{visualization}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{draw\PYGZus{}multilayer\PYGZus{}default}
\PYG{k+kn}{import}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{matplotlib}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{pyplot}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{as}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{plt}

\PYG{n}{fig}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{ax} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{plt}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{subplots}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{figsize}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mi}{12}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mi}{10}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{n}{plt}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{savefig}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{core\PYGZus{}network\PYGZus{}communities.png}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{dpi}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mi}{300}\PYG{p}{)}

\paragraph{Pattern: Per\sphinxhyphen{}Layer Top\sphinxhyphen{}K with Coverage (Multi\sphinxhyphen{}Layer Hub Detection)}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/query_with_dsl:pattern-per-layer-top-k-with-coverage-multi-layer-hub-detection}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Find nodes that are top\sphinxhyphen{}k hubs (by any centrality metric) \sphinxstylestrong{across all layers}. This pattern is essential for identifying nodes that maintain high influence in the entire multilayer structure, not just in isolated layers.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{The Problem:}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Traditional approaches require manual loops over layers:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Old approach: manual iteration}
\PYG{n}{layer\PYGZus{}top} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}
\PYG{k}{for} \PYG{n}{layer} \PYG{o+ow}{in} \PYG{n}{network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{layers}\PYG{p}{:}
    \PYG{n}{res} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{p}{(}
        \PYG{n}{Q}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{nodes}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
         \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{from\PYGZus{}layers}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{L}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{n+nb}{str}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{layer}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{)}
         \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{where}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{degree\PYGZus{}\PYGZus{}gt}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{p}{)}
         \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{compute}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{betweenness\PYGZus{}centrality}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
         \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{order\PYGZus{}by}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZhy{}betweenness\PYGZus{}centrality}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
         \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{limit}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mi}{5}\PYG{p}{)}
         \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{execute}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{)}
    \PYG{p}{)}
    \PYG{n}{layer\PYGZus{}top}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{n}{layer}\PYG{p}{]} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n+nb}{set}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{res}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{to\PYGZus{}pandas}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{id}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Find intersection}
\PYG{n}{multi\PYGZus{}hubs} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n+nb}{set}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{intersection}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{o}{*}\PYG{n}{layer\PYGZus{}top}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{values}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{The Solution: Grouping and Coverage API}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The new DSL supports per\sphinxhyphen{}layer operations in a single query:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{py3plex}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{core}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{random\PYGZus{}generators}
\PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{py3plex}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{dsl}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{Q}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{L}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Generate example network}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Use Cases:}
\begin{enumerate}
\sphinxsetlistlabels{\arabic}{enumi}{enumii}{}{.}%
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Identify persistent influencers}: Nodes that maintain high centrality across all contexts (layers)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Find layer specialists}: Nodes that are important in only one layer (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{mode="exact", k=1}})

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Detect multi\sphinxhyphen{}context bridges}: Nodes in top\sphinxhyphen{}k in at least 2 layers connect different contexts

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Community structure analysis}: Compare \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{mode="all"}} vs \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{mode="any"}} to understand layer cohesion

\end{enumerate}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Why This Pattern Matters:}

\sphinxAtStartPar
In real\sphinxhyphen{}world multilayer networks (social media, collaboration networks, biological systems), understanding \sphinxstylestrong{cross\sphinxhyphen{}layer} vs. \sphinxstylestrong{layer\sphinxhyphen{}specific} importance is crucial:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Email + Phone + Chat network}: Who are the omnipresent communicators vs. email\sphinxhyphen{}only specialists?

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Author collaboration network}: Who publishes top papers in multiple fields vs. specialists in one domain?

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Transportation network}: Which locations are hubs in all modes (bus, train, bike) vs. single\sphinxhyphen{}mode hubs?

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Performance Note:}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The per\sphinxhyphen{}layer computation is optimized: measures are computed on the selected nodes after layer filtering, and grouping operations leverage efficient dictionaries. For large networks (\textgreater{}100K nodes), consider filtering with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{where()}} before computing expensive metrics like betweenness centrality.


\subsubsection{Next Steps}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/query_with_dsl:next-steps}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Now that you understand the DSL, explore these related resources:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{DSL Reference} ({\hyperref[\detokenize{reference/dsl_reference::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{DSL Reference}}}}): Complete grammar, all operators, full list of built\sphinxhyphen{}in measures, and advanced features (EXPLAIN queries, parameter binding, custom operators)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Dplyr\sphinxhyphen{}Style Pipelines} ({\hyperref[\detokenize{how-to/build_pipelines::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{How to Build Analysis Pipelines with Dplyr\sphinxhyphen{}style Operations}}}}): Combine DSL queries with pipeline operations for more complex data transformation workflows. The pipeline API (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{nodes()}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{mutate()}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{arrange()}}) complements the DSL for when you need procedural transformations.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Community Detection} ({\hyperref[\detokenize{how-to/run_community_detection::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{How to Run Community Detection on Multilayer Networks}}}}): Use DSL queries to select nodes, then apply community detection algorithms. Pattern: query \(\rightarrow\) detect communities \(\rightarrow\) analyze community structure.

\item {}

\sphinxstylestrong{Network Dynamics} ({\hyperref[\detokenize{how-to/simulate_dynamics::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{How to Simulate Multilayer Dynamics}}}}): Run dynamics simulations on DSL\sphinxhyphen{}selected subnetworks. Pattern: query \(\rightarrow\) extract subnetwork \(\rightarrow\) simulate \(\rightarrow\) analyze outcomes.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Linting and Validation} ({\hyperref[\detokenize{reference/dsl_reference::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{DSL Reference}}}}): The DSL includes a linting subsystem (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{py3plex dsl\sphinxhyphen{}lint}}) that checks queries for errors, performance issues, and suggests optimizations. Use it to validate complex queries.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Examples Repository} ({\hyperref[\detokenize{examples/index::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{Examples \& Recipes}}}}): Full scripts showing DSL in context, including data loading, query composition, analysis, and visualization.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Key Takeaways:}
\begin{enumerate}
\sphinxsetlistlabels{\arabic}{enumi}{enumii}{}{.}%
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Use the builder API} (\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Q}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{L}}) for production code—it’s type\sphinxhyphen{}safe, refactorable, and IDE\sphinxhyphen{}friendly.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Filter early}: Add \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{where()}} clauses before \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{compute()}} for better performance on large networks.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Embrace pandas}: Use \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{.to\_pandas()}} for result analysis—it integrates seamlessly with the scientific Python stack.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Layer algebra is powerful}: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{L{[}"a"{]} + L{[}"b"{]}}} (union), \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{L{[}"a"{]} \& L{[}"b"{]}}} (intersection) enable sophisticated multilayer queries.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Temporal queries} require timestamped edges/nodes but unlock time\sphinxhyphen{}series network analysis.

\subsection{How to Build Analysis Pipelines with Dplyr\sphinxhyphen{}style Operations}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/build_pipelines:how-to-build-analysis-pipelines-with-dplyr-style-operations}}\label{\detokenize{how-to/build_pipelines::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Goal:} Chain operations to build reproducible analysis workflows.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Prerequisites:} A loaded network (see {\hyperref[\detokenize{how-to/load_and_build_networks::doc}]{\sphinxcrossref{\DUrole{doc}{How to Load and Build Networks}}}}).


\subsubsection{Basic Pipeline}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/build_pipelines:basic-pipeline}}

\paragraph{Node Operations}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/build_pipelines:node-operations}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{py3plex}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{core}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{multinet}
\PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{py3plex}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{graph\PYGZus{}ops}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{nodes}

\PYG{n}{network} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{multinet}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{multi\PYGZus{}layer\PYGZus{}network}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{load\PYGZus{}network}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{data.multiedgelist}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{input\PYGZus{}type}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{multiedgelist}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Build pipeline}
\PYG{n}{result} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{p}{(}
    \PYG{n}{nodes}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{)}
    \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{filter}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{k}{lambda} \PYG{n}{n}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{n}{n}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{degree}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{]} \PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}} \PYG{l+m+mi}{2}\PYG{p}{)}
    \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{mutate}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{score}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{k}{lambda} \PYG{n}{n}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{n}{n}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{degree}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{]} \PYG{o}{*} \PYG{l+m+mi}{2}\PYG{p}{)}
    \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{arrange}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{degree}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{reverse}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{k+kc}{True}\PYG{p}{)}
    \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{to\PYGZus{}pandas}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{p}{)}

\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{result}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{head}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsubsection{Available Operations}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/build_pipelines:available-operations}}

\paragraph{filter()}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/build_pipelines:filter}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Select nodes based on condition:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{result} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{p}{(}
    \PYG{n}{nodes}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{)}
    \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{filter}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{k}{lambda} \PYG{n}{n}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{n}{n}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{layer}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{]} \PYG{o}{==} \PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{friends}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
    \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{filter}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{k}{lambda} \PYG{n}{n}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{n}{n}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{degree}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{]} \PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}} \PYG{l+m+mi}{5}\PYG{p}{)}
    \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{to\PYGZus{}pandas}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\paragraph{mutate()}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/build_pipelines:mutate}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Add or modify columns:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{result} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{p}{(}
    \PYG{n}{nodes}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{)}
    \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{mutate}\PYG{p}{(}
        \PYG{n}{degree\PYGZus{}squared}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{k}{lambda} \PYG{n}{n}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{n}{n}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{degree}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{]} \PYG{o}{*}\PYG{o}{*} \PYG{l+m+mi}{2}\PYG{p}{,}
        \PYG{n}{is\PYGZus{}hub}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{k}{lambda} \PYG{n}{n}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{n}{n}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{degree}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{]} \PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}} \PYG{l+m+mi}{10}
    \PYG{p}{)}
    \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{to\PYGZus{}pandas}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\paragraph{select()}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/build_pipelines:select}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Choose specific columns:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{result} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{p}{(}
    \PYG{n}{nodes}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{)}

    \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{to\PYGZus{}pandas}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\label{\detokenize{how-to/build_pipelines:arrange}}
\sphinxAtStartPar

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]

    \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{to\PYGZus{}pandas}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{p}{)}

\paragraph{group\_by() and summarize()}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/build_pipelines:group-by-and-summarize}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Aggregate data:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{result} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{p}{(}
    \PYG{n}{nodes}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{)}
    \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{group\PYGZus{}by}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{layer}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}

        \PYG{n}{max\PYGZus{}degree}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{k}{lambda} \PYG{n}{g}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{n}{g}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{degree}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{max}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{,}
        \PYG{n}{count}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{k}{lambda} \PYG{n}{g}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{n+nb}{len}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{g}\PYG{p}{)}
    \PYG{p}{)}
    \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{to\PYGZus{}pandas}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\subsubsection{Complex Pipelines}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/build_pipelines:complex-pipelines}}

\paragraph{Multi\sphinxhyphen{}Step Analysis}
\label{\detokenize{how-to/build_pipelines:multi-step-analysis}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n}{result} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{p}{(}
    \PYG{n}{nodes}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{)}
    \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Step 1: Filter active nodes}
    \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{filter}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{k}{lambda} \PYG{n}{n}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{n}{n}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{layer\PYGZus{}count}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{]} \PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}} \PYG{l+m+mi}{1}\PYG{p}{)}
    \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Step 2: Add computed score}

        \PYG{n}{activity\PYGZus{}score}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{k}{lambda} \PYG{n}{n}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{n}{n}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{degree}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{]} \PYG{o}{*} \PYG{n}{n}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{layer\PYGZus{}count}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{]}
    \PYG{p}{)}
    \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Step 3: Filter by score}
    \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{filter}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{k}{lambda} \PYG{n}{n}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{n}{n}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{activity\PYGZus{}score}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{]} \PYG{o}{\PYGZgt{}} \PYG{l+m+mi}{20}\PYG{p}{)}
    \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Step 4: Sort by score}

    \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Step 5: Get top 20}
    \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{head}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mi}{20}\PYG{p}{)}
    \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Convert to pandas}
    \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{to\PYGZus{}pandas}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

    \PYG{p}{)}
    \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{arrange}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{centrality\PYGZus{}rank}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{reverse}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{k+kc}{True}\PYG{p}{)}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]

\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{n}{sir}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{set\PYGZus{}seed}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mi}{42}\PYG{p}{)}

\subsubsection{What are Multilayer Networks?}
\label{\detokenize{concepts/multilayer_networks_101:what-are-multilayer-networks}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
A \sphinxstylestrong{multilayer network} models systems with multiple types of relationships, node types, or interaction contexts.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Example:} A researcher’s social world includes coauthors, colleagues, students, and Twitter followers. These are different relationship types with different meanings. A multilayer network keeps them as separate \sphinxstylestrong{layers} rather than flattening into one graph.

\sphinxstylestrong{Multiple networks where nodes depend on each other.}
