\index{load\_network() (py3plex.core.multinet.multi\_layer\_network method)@\spxentry{load\_network()}\spxextra{py3plex.core.multinet.multi\_layer\_network method}}

\begin{savenotes}\begin{fulllineitems}
\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{reference/api_index:py3plex.core.multinet.multi_layer_network.load_network}}
\pysigstartsignatures
\pysiglinewithargsret
{\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{load\_network}}}
{\sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{input\_file}\DUrole{p}{:}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{n}{str\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{p}{|}\DUrole{w}{ }None}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{o}{=}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{default_value}{None}}\sphinxparamcomma \sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{directed}\DUrole{p}{:}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{n}{bool}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{o}{=}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{default_value}{False}}\sphinxparamcomma \sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{input\_type}\DUrole{p}{:}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{n}{str}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{o}{=}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{default_value}{\textquotesingle{}gml\textquotesingle{}}}\sphinxparamcomma \sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{label\_delimiter}\DUrole{p}{:}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{n}{str}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{o}{=}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{default_value}{\textquotesingle{}\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}\sphinxhyphen{}\textquotesingle{}}}}
{{ $\rightarrow$ {\hyperref[\detokenize{reference/api_index:py3plex.core.multinet.multi_layer_network}]{\sphinxcrossref{multi\_layer\_network}}}}}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Load a network from file.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This method loads and prepares a given network. The behavior depends on
the \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{network\_type}} set during initialization:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{multilayer}: Network is loaded as\sphinxhyphen{}is. No automatic edges are added.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{multiplex}: After loading, coupling edges are automatically created
between each node and its counterparts in other layers. These edges
have type=’coupling’ and can be filtered via get\_edges().

\end{itemize}
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Parameters}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{input\_file}} \textendash{} Path to the network file to load

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{directed}} \textendash{} Whether the network is directed

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{input\_type}} \textendash{} Format of the input file. Supported values:
\sphinxhyphen{} ‘gml’: Graph Modeling Language format
\sphinxhyphen{} ‘graphml’: GraphML XML format
\sphinxhyphen{} ‘edgelist’: Simple edge list (source target {[}weight{]})
\sphinxhyphen{} ‘multiedgelist’: Multilayer edge list (node1 layer1 node2 layer2 weight)
\sphinxhyphen{} ‘multiplex\_edges’: Multiplex format (layer node1 node2 weight)
\sphinxhyphen{} ‘multiplex\_folder’: Folder with layer files
\sphinxhyphen{} ‘gpickle’: Python pickle format
\sphinxhyphen{} ‘nx’: NetworkX graph object
\sphinxhyphen{} ‘sparse’: Sparse matrix format

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{label\_delimiter}} \textendash{} Delimiter used to separate layer names in node labels

\end{itemize}

\sphinxlineitem{Returns}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Self for method chaining. Populates self.core\_network, self.labels,
and self.activity.

\end{description}\end{quote}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
For multiplex networks, use input\_type=’multiplex\_edges’ or
‘multiplex\_folder’ with network\_type=’multiplex’ to get automatic
coupling edges.
\end{sphinxadmonition}
\subsubsection*{Examples}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Load multilayer network (no automatic coupling)}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{n}{net} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{multi\PYGZus{}layer\PYGZus{}network}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network\PYGZus{}type}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{multilayer}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{n}{net}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{load\PYGZus{}network}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{data.gml}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{input\PYGZus{}type}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{gml}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{)}  
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Load multiplex network (automatic coupling edges)}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{n}{net} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{multi\PYGZus{}layer\PYGZus{}network}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network\PYGZus{}type}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{multiplex}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{n}{net}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{load\PYGZus{}network}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{data.edges}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{input\PYGZus{}type}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{multiplex\PYGZus{}edges}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{)}  
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\end{fulllineitems}\end{savenotes}

A generic networkx function wrapper.
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Parameters}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{method}} (\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{str}}) \textendash{} Name of the NetworkX function to call (e.g., ‘degree\_centrality’, ‘betweenness\_centrality’)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{kwargs}} (\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{dict}}\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{, }}\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{optional}}) \textendash{} Keyword arguments to pass to the NetworkX function.
For example, for betweenness\_centrality you can pass:
\sphinxhyphen{} weight: Edge attribute to use as weight
\sphinxhyphen{} normalized: Whether to normalize betweenness values
\sphinxhyphen{} distance: Edge attribute to use as distance (for closeness\_centrality)

\end{itemize}

\sphinxlineitem{Returns}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The result of the NetworkX function call.

\sphinxlineitem{Raises}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{AttributeError}} \textendash{} If the specified method does not exist in NetworkX.

\end{description}\end{quote}
\subsubsection*{Example}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\# Unweighted betweenness centrality
centralities = network.monoplex\_nx\_wrapper(“betweenness\_centrality”)

\sphinxAtStartPar
\# Weighted betweenness centrality
centralities = network.monoplex\_nx\_wrapper(“betweenness\_centrality”, kwargs=\{“weight”: “weight”\})

\sphinxAtStartPar
\# With multiple parameters
centralities = network.monoplex\_nx\_wrapper(“betweenness\_centrality”,
\begin{quote}

\sphinxAtStartPar
kwargs=\{“weight”: “weight”, “normalized”: True\})
\end{quote}

\end{fulllineitems}\end{savenotes}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Remove all edges from separate layer graphs while keeping nodes.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This method creates empty copies of each layer graph with all nodes intact
but no edges. Useful for reconstructing networks with different edge sets
or for temporal network analysis.
\subsubsection*{Notes}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Requires split\_to\_layers() to be called first

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Stores empty layer graphs in self.tmp\_layers

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Original graphs in self.separate\_layers remain unchanged

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
All nodes and their attributes are preserved

\end{itemize}
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Raises}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{RuntimeError}} \textendash{} If split\_to\_layers() hasn’t been called yet

\end{description}\end{quote}


\begin{sphinxseealso}{See also:}

\sphinxAtStartPar
split\_to\_layers: Must be called before this method
fill\_tmp\_with\_edges: Add edges back to emptied layers


\end{sphinxseealso}


\end{fulllineitems}\end{savenotes}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Save the network to a file in various formats.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This method exports the multilayer network to different file formats
for persistence, sharing, or use with other tools.
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Parameters}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{output\_file}} \textendash{} Path where the network should be saved

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{output\_type}} \textendash{} Format for saving (‘edgelist’, ‘multiedgelist’,
‘multiedgelist\_encoded’, or ‘gpickle’)

\end{itemize}

\end{description}\end{quote}
\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Supported Formats:}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
‘edgelist’: Simple edge list format (standard NetworkX)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
‘multiedgelist’: Multilayer edge list with layer information

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
‘multiedgelist\_encoded’: Multilayer edge list with integer encoding

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
‘gpickle’: Python pickle format (preserves all attributes)

\end{itemize}

\end{description}
\subsubsection*{Examples}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{n}{net} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{multi\PYGZus{}layer\PYGZus{}network}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{n}{net}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{add\PYGZus{}nodes}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{source}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{A}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{type}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{layer1}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{n}{net}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{add\PYGZus{}edges}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{source}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{A}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{target}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{B}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{g+gp}{... }                \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{source\PYGZus{}type}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{layer1}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{target\PYGZus{}type}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{layer1}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{n}{net}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{save\PYGZus{}network}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{network.txt}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{output\PYGZus{}type}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{multiedgelist}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} For faster I/O with all metadata preserved}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{n}{net}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{save\PYGZus{}network}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{network.gpickle}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{output\PYGZus{}type}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{gpickle}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\subsubsection*{Notes}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
‘gpickle’ format preserves all node/edge attributes

\item {}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar

\end{itemize}

\begin{savenotes}\begin{fulllineitems}

\pysigstartsignatures

{\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{serialize\_to\_edgelist}}}
{\sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{edgelist\_file}\DUrole{o}{=}\DUrole{default_value}{\textquotesingle{}./tmp/tmpedgelist.txt\textquotesingle{}}}\sphinxparamcomma \sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{tmp\_folder}\DUrole{o}{=}\DUrole{default_value}{\textquotesingle{}tmp\textquotesingle{}}}\sphinxparamcomma \sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{out\_folder}\DUrole{o}{=}\DUrole{default_value}{\textquotesingle{}out\textquotesingle{}}}\sphinxparamcomma \sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{multiplex}\DUrole{o}{=}\DUrole{default_value}{False}}}
{}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Serialize the multilayer network to an edgelist file.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Converts the network to a numeric edgelist format suitable for external tools
and algorithms that require integer node/layer identifiers.
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Parameters}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{edgelist\_file}} \textendash{} Path to output edgelist file (default: “./tmp/tmpedgelist.txt”)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{tmp\_folder}} \textendash{} Temporary folder for intermediate files (default: “tmp”)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{out\_folder}} \textendash{} Output folder for results (default: “out”)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{multiplex}} \textendash{} If True, use multiplex format (node layer node layer weight)
If False, use simple edgelist format (node1 node2 weight)

\end{itemize}

\sphinxlineitem{Returns}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Inverse node mapping (numeric\_id \sphinxhyphen{}\textgreater{} original\_node\_tuple)}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Use this to decode results from external algorithms

\end{description}


\sphinxlineitem{Return type}
\sphinxAtStartPar
dict

\end{description}\end{quote}
\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{File Formats:}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Multiplex format: node1\_id layer1\_id node2\_id layer2\_id weight

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Simple format: node1\_id node2\_id weight

\end{itemize}

\end{description}
\subsubsection*{Notes}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Creates tmp\_folder and out\_folder if they don’t exist

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Nodes are mapped to sequential integers starting from 0

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Layers are mapped to sequential integers starting from 0 (multiplex mode)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
All edges have weight 1 unless explicitly specified

\end{itemize}
\subsubsection*{Examples}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Example requires file output \sphinxhyphen{} for illustration only.

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{n}{net} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{multi\PYGZus{}layer\PYGZus{}network}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}  
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} ... build network ...}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{n}{node\PYGZus{}mapping} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{net}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{serialize\PYGZus{}to\PYGZus{}edgelist}\PYG{p}{(}  
\PYG{g+gp}{... }    \PYG{n}{edgelist\PYGZus{}file}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{network.txt}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{g+gp}{... }    \PYG{n}{multiplex}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{k+kc}{True}
\PYG{g+gp}{... }\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Use node\PYGZus{}mapping to decode results}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{n}{original\PYGZus{}node} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{node\PYGZus{}mapping}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+m+mi}{0}\PYG{p}{]}  \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Get original node for id 0  }

\begin{savenotes}\begin{fulllineitems}

{\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{to\_homogeneous\_hypergraph}}}
{}
{}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Transform a multiplex network into a homogeneous graph using incidence gadget encoding.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This method encodes the multiplex structure where each layer is represented by
a unique prime number signature. Each edge becomes an edge\sphinxhyphen{}node connected to
its endpoints and a cycle of length prime\sphinxhyphen{}1 that encodes the layer.
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Returns}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{tuple (H, node\_mapping, edge\_info)} \textendash{}
\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{H}{[}networkx.Graph{]}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Homogeneous unlabeled graph encoding the multiplex structure.

\sphinxlineitem{node\_mapping}{[}dict{]}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Maps each original node to its vertex\sphinxhyphen{}node in H.

\sphinxlineitem{edge\_info}{[}dict{]}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Mapping from each edge\sphinxhyphen{}node in H to its (layer, endpoints) tuple.

\end{description}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleemphasis{Examples} \textendash{} Example requires sympy dependency \sphinxhyphen{} for illustration only.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{\textgreater{}\textgreater{}\textgreater{} network = multi\_layer\_network(directed=False)  \# doctest} (\sphinxstyleemphasis{+SKIP})

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{\textgreater{}\textgreater{}\textgreater{} network.add\_nodes({[}\{‘source’} (\sphinxstyleemphasis{‘1’, ‘type’: ‘A’\}, \{‘source’: ‘2’, ‘type’: ‘A’\}{]}, input\_type=’dict’)  \# doctest: +SKIP})

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{\textgreater{}\textgreater{}\textgreater{} network.add\_edges({[}\{‘source’} (\sphinxstyleemphasis{‘1’, ‘target’: ‘2’, ‘source\_type’: ‘A’, ‘target\_type’: ‘A’\}{]}, input\_type=’dict’)  \# doctest: +SKIP})

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{\textgreater{}\textgreater{}\textgreater{} H, node\_map, edge\_info = network.to\_homogeneous\_hypergraph()  \# doctest} (\sphinxstyleemphasis{+SKIP})

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{\textgreater{}\textgreater{}\textgreater{} print(f”Homogeneous graph has \{len(H.nodes())\} nodes”)  \# doctest} (\sphinxstyleemphasis{+SKIP})

\end{itemize}


\end{description}\end{quote}
\subsubsection*{Notes}

\sphinxAtStartPar
This transformation uses prime\sphinxhyphen{}based signatures to encode layers:
\sphinxhyphen{} Each layer is assigned a unique prime number (2, 3, 5, 7, …)
\sphinxhyphen{} Each edge in layer with prime p is connected to a cycle of length p
\sphinxhyphen{} The cycle structure uniquely identifies the layer

\end{fulllineitems}\end{savenotes}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Convert the multilayer network to a NetworkX graph.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Returns a copy of the core network as a NetworkX graph. The returned graph
preserves all node and edge attributes, including layer information for
multilayer networks (where nodes are typically (node\_id, layer) tuples).
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Returns}
\sphinxAtStartPar
A NetworkX graph (MultiGraph or MultiDiGraph depending on network type)

\sphinxlineitem{Return type}
\sphinxAtStartPar
nx.Graph

\end{description}\end{quote}
\subsubsection*{Examples}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{n}{net} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{multi\PYGZus{}layer\PYGZus{}network}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{directed}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{k+kc}{False}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{n}{net}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{add\PYGZus{}nodes}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{source}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{A}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{type}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{layer1}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{n}{nx\PYGZus{}graph} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{net}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{to\PYGZus{}networkx}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{n+nb}{print}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n+nb}{type}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{nx\PYGZus{}graph}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{g+go}{\PYGZlt{}class \PYGZsq{}networkx.classes.multigraph.MultiGraph\PYGZsq{}\PYGZgt{}}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\subsubsection*{Notes}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
For multilayer networks, nodes are tuples: (node\_id, layer)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
All edge attributes (weight, type, etc.) are preserved

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
The returned graph is a copy, not a reference

\end{itemize}

\end{fulllineitems}\end{savenotes}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Visualize the multilayer network.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Supports multiple visualization styles:
\sphinxhyphen{} ‘diagonal’: Layer\sphinxhyphen{}centric diagonal layout with inter\sphinxhyphen{}layer edges

\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Performance Notes:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
For large networks (\textgreater{}500 nodes), visualization performance may degrade:
\sphinxhyphen{} Layout computation can be slow (O(n\(\sp{\text{2}}\)) for force\sphinxhyphen{}directed layouts)
\sphinxhyphen{} Rendering many edges is memory and CPU intensive
\sphinxhyphen{} Consider filtering or sampling for exploratory visualization
\sphinxhyphen{} Use simpler layouts or increase layout iteration limits

\sphinxAtStartPar
Approximate rendering times on typical hardware:
\sphinxhyphen{} 100 nodes: \textless{}1 second
\sphinxhyphen{} 500 nodes: 5\sphinxhyphen{}10 seconds
\sphinxhyphen{} 1000 nodes: 30\sphinxhyphen{}60 seconds
\sphinxhyphen{} 5000+ nodes: Several minutes, may run out of memory

\end{description}

\sphinxAtStartPar
This method is a high\sphinxhyphen{}level wrapper for Ricci\sphinxhyphen{}flow\sphinxhyphen{}based visualization

\sphinxAtStartPar

\sphinxAtStartPar
Visualize individual layers using Ricci\sphinxhyphen{}flow\sphinxhyphen{}based layouts.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This method creates visualizations of individual layers with layouts
derived from Ricci flow. Layers can share a common coordinate system
(for easier comparison) or have independent layouts.
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Parameters}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{layers}} \textendash{} List of layer identifiers to visualize. If None, uses all layers.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{alpha}} \textendash{} Ollivier\sphinxhyphen{}Ricci parameter. Default: 0.5.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{iterations}} \textendash{} Number of Ricci flow iterations. Default: 10.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{layout\_type}} \textendash{} Layout algorithm. Default: “mds”.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{share\_layout}} \textendash{} If True, use shared coordinates across layers. Default: True.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{**kwargs}} \textendash{} Additional arguments passed to visualize\_multilayer\_ricci\_layers.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxlineitem{Returns}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Tuple of (figure, layer\_positions\_dict).

\sphinxlineitem{Raises}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{RicciBackendNotAvailable}} \textendash{} If GraphRicciCurvature is not installed.

\end{description}\end{quote}
\subsubsection*{Examples}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{layout\_type}} \textendash{} Layout algorithm. Default: “mds”.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar

\index{parse\_edgelist\_multi\_types() (in module py3plex.core.parsers)@\spxentry{parse\_edgelist\_multi\_types()}\spxextra{in module py3plex.core.parsers}}

\begin{savenotes}\begin{fulllineitems}

\pysigstartsignatures
\pysiglinewithargsret
{\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{py3plex.core.parsers.}}\sphinxbfcode{\sphinxupquote{parse\_edgelist\_multi\_types}}}
{\sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{input\_name}\DUrole{p}{:}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{n}{str}}\sphinxparamcomma \sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{directed}\DUrole{p}{:}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{n}{bool}}}
{{ $\rightarrow$ Tuple\DUrole{p}{{[}}MultiGraph\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{p}{|}\DUrole{w}{ }MultiDiGraph\DUrole{p}{,}\DUrole{w}{ }None\DUrole{p}{{]}}}}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Parse an edgelist file with multiple edge types.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Reads a text file where each line represents an edge, optionally with weights
and edge types. Lines starting with ‘\#’ are treated as comments.
\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{File Format:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
node1 node2 {[}weight{]} {[}edge\_type{]}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Lines starting with ‘\#’ are ignored (comments)

\end{description}
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Parameters}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{input\_name}} \textendash{} Path to edgelist file

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{directed}} \textendash{} Whether to create a directed graph

\end{itemize}

\sphinxlineitem{Returns}
\sphinxAtStartPar
(parsed\_graph, None for labels)

\sphinxlineitem{Return type}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Tuple{[}Union{[}nx.MultiGraph, nx.MultiDiGraph{]}, None{]}

\end{description}\end{quote}
\subsubsection*{Notes}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
All nodes are assigned to a “null” layer

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Default weight is 1 if not specified

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Edge type is optional (4th column)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Handles both 2\sphinxhyphen{}column (node pairs) and 3+ column formats

\end{itemize}
\subsubsection*{Examples}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} File content:}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} A B 1.0 friendship}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} B C 2.0 collaboration}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{n}{graph}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{\PYGZus{}} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{parse\PYGZus{}edgelist\PYGZus{}multi\PYGZus{}types}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{edges.txt}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{directed}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{k+kc}{False}\PYG{p}{)}  
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\end{fulllineitems}\end{savenotes}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Parse a multiplex edgelist file where each line specifies layer and edge.
\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{File Format:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
layer node1 node2 {[}weight{]}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Each line: layer\_id source\_node target\_node {[}optional\_weight{]}

\end{description}
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Parameters}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{input\_name}} \textendash{} Path to multiplex edgelist file

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{directed}} \textendash{} Whether to create a directed graph

\end{itemize}

\sphinxlineitem{Returns}
\sphinxAtStartPar
(parsed\_graph, None for labels)

\sphinxlineitem{Return type}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Tuple{[}Union{[}nx.MultiGraph, nx.MultiDiGraph{]}, None{]}

\end{description}\end{quote}
\subsubsection*{Notes}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Each edge belongs to a specific layer (first column)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Nodes are represented as (node\_id, layer) tuples

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Default weight is 1 if not specified

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
All edges have type=’default’ attribute

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Automatically couples nodes across layers for multiplex structure

\end{itemize}
\subsubsection*{Examples}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} File content:}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} layer1 A B 1.5}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} layer2 A B 2.0}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} layer1 B C 1.0}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{n}{graph}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{\PYGZus{}} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{parse\PYGZus{}multiplex\PYGZus{}edges}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{multiplex.txt}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{directed}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{k+kc}{False}\PYG{p}{)}  
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Creates nodes: (A, layer1), (A, layer2), (B, layer1), etc.}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\end{fulllineitems}\end{savenotes}

\sphinxAtStartPar

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
activity.txt: Optional temporal activity (format: node1 node2 timestamp layer\_name)

\end{itemize}

\end{description}

\sphinxlineitem{Parameters}\begin{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Union{[}nx.MultiGraph, nx.MultiDiGraph{]}: Parsed multilayer graph

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
None: Placeholder for labels (not used)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
pd.DataFrame: Time series activity data (empty if no activity.txt)

\end{itemize}


\sphinxlineitem{Return type}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Tuple containing

\end{description}\end{quote}
\subsubsection*{Notes}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Uses glob to find files with specific extensions

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Layer mapping is built from layers.txt

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Activity data is optional and returned as pandas DataFrame

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Nodes are represented as (node\_id, layer\_id) tuples

\end{itemize}

\sphinxlineitem{Return type}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Tuple{[}nx.Graph, None{]}

\end{description}\end{quote}
\subsubsection*{Notes}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Currently always returns nx.Graph (undirected) regardless of directed parameter

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Edge tag is stored in edge ‘type’ attribute

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Default weight is 1 if not specified (4th column)

\end{itemize}

\item {}

\item {}

\end{itemize}

\end{description}

\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Generate a simple multiplex multilayer stochastic block model (SBM) network.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This function creates a multilayer network with:
\sphinxhyphen{} \sphinxtitleref{n\_nodes} nodes shared across all layers,
\sphinxhyphen{} \sphinxtitleref{n\_layers} layers,
\sphinxhyphen{} \sphinxtitleref{n\_blocks} latent communities (blocks),
\sphinxhyphen{} within\sphinxhyphen{}block edge probability \sphinxtitleref{p\_in},
\sphinxhyphen{} between\sphinxhyphen{}block edge probability \sphinxtitleref{p\_out},
\sphinxhyphen{} optional diagonal inter\sphinxhyphen{}layer coupling with probability \sphinxtitleref{coupling}
\begin{quote}

\sphinxAtStartPar
between replicas of the same node across layers.
\end{quote}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The block memberships are shared across layers in this simple model,
and the same block probability matrix is used for all layers.
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Parameters}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{n\_layers}} (\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{int}}) \textendash{} Number of layers.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{n\_nodes}} (\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{int}}) \textendash{} Number of nodes (shared across all layers).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{n\_blocks}} (\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{int}}) \textendash{} Number of blocks (communities).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{p\_in}} (\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{float}}) \textendash{} Edge probability for edges within the same block.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{p\_out}} (\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{float}}) \textendash{} Edge probability for edges between different blocks.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{coupling}} (\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{float}}\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{, }}\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{optional}}) \textendash{} Probability of inter\sphinxhyphen{}layer edges between replicas of the same node
in different layers. Defaults to 0.0 (no inter\sphinxhyphen{}layer edges).

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{directed}} (\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{bool}}\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{, }}\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{optional}}) \textendash{} Whether to generate directed layers. Defaults to False.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{seed}} (\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{int}}\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{, }}\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{optional}}) \textendash{} Random seed for reproducibility.

\end{itemize}

\sphinxlineitem{Returns}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{network} (\sphinxstyleemphasis{multi\_layer\_network}) \textendash{} The generated multilayer network.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{metadata} (\sphinxstyleemphasis{SBMMetadata}) \textendash{} Ground\sphinxhyphen{}truth metadata containing block memberships and block matrix.

\end{itemize}


\end{description}\end{quote}
\subsubsection*{Notes}
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Node IDs are strings “v0”, “v1”, …, “v\{n\_nodes\sphinxhyphen{}1\}”.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Layer names are strings “L0”, “L1”, …, “L\{n\_layers\sphinxhyphen{}1\}”.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Edges are inserted via the py3plex list\sphinxhyphen{}based API:
{[}src\_node, src\_layer, dst\_node, dst\_layer, weight{]}.

\end{itemize}
\subsubsection*{Examples}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{py3plex}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{core}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{random\PYGZus{}generators}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{random\PYGZus{}multilayer\PYGZus{}SBM}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{n}{net}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{meta} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{random\PYGZus{}multilayer\PYGZus{}SBM}\PYG{p}{(}
\PYG{g+gp}{... }    \PYG{n}{n\PYGZus{}layers}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mi}{3}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{n\PYGZus{}nodes}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mi}{20}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{n\PYGZus{}blocks}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mi}{2}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{g+gp}{... }    \PYG{n}{p\PYGZus{}in}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mf}{0.5}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{p\PYGZus{}out}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mf}{0.05}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{coupling}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mf}{0.1}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{seed}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mi}{42}
\PYG{g+gp}{... }\PYG{p}{)}

and other configurable aspects of the library. Users can override these
settings by modifying the values after import.

{\sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{relative\_path}\DUrole{p}{:}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{n}{str}}}
{{ $\rightarrow$ str}}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Get the absolute path to a data file in the repository.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This function searches for data files in multiple locations to support both:
\sphinxhyphen{} Running examples from a cloned repository
\sphinxhyphen{} Running scripts/notebooks from any directory with datasets locally available

\sphinxAtStartPar
Search order:
1. Relative to the calling script’s directory (for examples in cloned repo)
2. Relative to current working directory (for notebooks/user scripts)
3. Relative to py3plex package location (for editable installs)
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Parameters}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{relative\_path}} \textendash{} Path relative to repository root (e.g., “datasets/intact02.gpickle”)

\sphinxlineitem{Returns}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Absolute path to the file

\sphinxlineitem{Return type}
\sphinxAtStartPar
str

\sphinxlineitem{Raises}
\sphinxAtStartPar
{\hyperref[\detokenize{reference/api_index:py3plex.exceptions.Py3plexIOError}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{Py3plexIOError}}}}} \textendash{} If the file cannot be found in any search location

\end{description}\end{quote}
\subsubsection*{Examples}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{py3plex}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{utils}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{get\PYGZus{}data\PYGZus{}path}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{n}{path} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{get\PYGZus{}data\PYGZus{}path}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{datasets/intact02.gpickle}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{n}{os}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{path}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{exists}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{path}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{g+go}{True}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
When py3plex is installed via pip, datasets are not included in the package.
Users should either:
\sphinxhyphen{} Clone the repository and run examples from there
\sphinxhyphen{} Download datasets separately and place them relative to their scripts
\sphinxhyphen{} Use current working directory with datasets folder
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\end{fulllineitems}\end{savenotes}

{{ $\rightarrow$ Generator}}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Get a NumPy random number generator with optional seed.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This provides a unified interface for random state management across
the library, ensuring reproducibility when a seed is provided.
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Parameters}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{seed}} \textendash{} Random seed for reproducibility. Can be:
\sphinxhyphen{} None: Use default unseeded generator
\sphinxhyphen{} int: Seed value for the generator
\sphinxhyphen{} np.random.Generator: Pass through existing generator

\sphinxlineitem{Returns}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Initialized random number generator

\sphinxlineitem{Return type}
\sphinxAtStartPar
np.random.Generator

\end{description}\end{quote}
\subsubsection*{Examples}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{n}{rng} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{get\PYGZus{}rng}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mi}{42}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{n}{rng}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{random}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}  \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Reproducible random number}
\PYG{g+go}{0.7739560485559633}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{n}{rng1} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{get\PYGZus{}rng}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mi}{42}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{n}{rng2} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{get\PYGZus{}rng}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mi}{42}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{n}{rng1}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{random}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)} \PYG{o}{==} \PYG{n}{rng2}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{random}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{g+go}{True}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{n}{existing\PYGZus{}rng} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{np}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{random}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{default\PYGZus{}rng}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mi}{123}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{n}{rng} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{get\PYGZus{}rng}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{existing\PYGZus{}rng}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{n}{rng} \PYG{o+ow}{is} \PYG{n}{existing\PYGZus{}rng}
\PYG{g+go}{True}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Contracts:}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Postcondition: result is a NumPy random Generator

\end{itemize}

\end{description}

\begin{sphinxadmonition}{note}{Note:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Uses numpy.random.Generator (modern API introduced in NumPy 1.17)
rather than the legacy numpy.random.RandomState API.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Negative seeds are converted to positive values by taking absolute value
to ensure compatibility with NumPy’s SeedSequence.
\end{sphinxadmonition}

\end{fulllineitems}\end{savenotes}

\index{module@\spxentry{module}!py3plex.exceptions@\spxentry{py3plex.exceptions}}\index{py3plex.exceptions@\spxentry{py3plex.exceptions}!module@\spxentry{module}}\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{reference/api_index:module-py3plex.exceptions}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Custom exception types for the py3plex library.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This module defines domain\sphinxhyphen{}specific exceptions to provide clear error messages
and enable better error handling throughout the library.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Py3plex follows Rust’s approach to error messages:
\sphinxhyphen{} Clear, descriptive error messages
\sphinxhyphen{} Error codes (e.g., PX101, PX201)
\sphinxhyphen{} Helpful suggestions for fixing issues
\sphinxhyphen{} “Did you mean?” suggestions for typos
\sphinxhyphen{} Context showing the relevant location in files

\subsubsection{Domain\sphinxhyphen{}Specific Language (DSL)}
\label{\detokenize{reference/api_index:module-py3plex.dsl}}\label{\detokenize{reference/api_index:domain-specific-language-dsl}}\index{module@\spxentry{module}!py3plex.dsl@\spxentry{py3plex.dsl}}\index{py3plex.dsl@\spxentry{py3plex.dsl}!module@\spxentry{module}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
DSL v2 for Multilayer Network Queries.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This module provides a Domain\sphinxhyphen{}Specific Language (DSL) version 2 for querying and
analyzing multilayer networks. DSL v2 introduces:
\begin{enumerate}
\sphinxsetlistlabels{\arabic}{enumi}{enumii}{}{.}%
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Unified AST representation

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Pythonic builder API (Q, L, Param)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Multilayer\sphinxhyphen{}specific abstractions (layer algebra, intralayer/interlayer)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Improved ergonomics (ORDER BY, LIMIT, EXPLAIN, rich results)

\end{enumerate}

\sphinxAtStartPar
DSL Extensions (v2.1):
5. Network comparison (C.compare())
6. Null models (N.model())
7. Path queries (P.shortest(), P.random\_walk())
8. Plugin system for user\sphinxhyphen{}defined operators (@dsl\_operator)
\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Example Usage:}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{py3plex}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{dsl}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{Q}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{L}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{Param}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{C}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{N}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{P}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Build a query using the builder API}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{n}{q} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{p}{(}
\PYG{g+gp}{... }    \PYG{n}{Q}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{nodes}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{g+gp}{... }     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{from\PYGZus{}layers}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{L}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{social}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{]} \PYG{o}{+} \PYG{n}{L}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{work}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{g+gp}{... }     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{where}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{intralayer}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{k+kc}{True}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{degree\PYGZus{}\PYGZus{}gt}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mi}{5}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{g+gp}{... }     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{compute}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{betweenness\PYGZus{}centrality}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{alias}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{bc}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{g+gp}{... }     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{order\PYGZus{}by}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{bc}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{desc}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{k+kc}{True}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{g+gp}{... }     \PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{limit}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mi}{20}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{g+gp}{... }\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Execute the query}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{n}{result} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{q}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{execute}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{k}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mi}{5}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{n}{df} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{result}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{to\PYGZus{}pandas}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Compare two networks}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{n}{comparison} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{C}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{compare}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{baseline}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{treatment}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{using}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{multiplex\PYGZus{}jaccard}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{execute}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{networks}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Generate null models}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{n}{nullmodels} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{N}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{configuration}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{samples}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mi}{100}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{seed}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+m+mi}{42}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{execute}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Find paths}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{n}{paths} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{P}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{shortest}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{Alice}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{Bob}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{crossing\PYGZus{}layers}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{execute}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{network}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Define custom operators}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{n+nd}{@dsl\PYGZus{}operator}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{my\PYGZus{}measure}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{g+gp}{... }\PYG{k}{def}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nf}{my\PYGZus{}custom\PYGZus{}measure}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{context}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{n}{param}\PYG{p}{:} \PYG{n+nb}{float} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{l+m+mf}{1.0}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{:}
\PYG{g+gp}{... }    \PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Use context.graph, context.current\PYGZus{}layers, etc.}
\PYG{g+gp}{... }    \PYG{k}{return} \PYG{n}{result}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxlineitem{The DSL also supports a string syntax:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
SELECT nodes
FROM LAYER(“social”) + LAYER(“work”)
WHERE intralayer AND degree \textgreater{} 5
COMPUTE betweenness\_centrality AS bc
ORDER BY bc DESC
LIMIT 20
TO pandas

\end{description}

\sphinxAtStartPar
All frontends (string DSL, builder API) compile into a single AST which is
executed by the same engine, ensuring consistent behavior.

with the metric names.

closeness (or closeness\_centrality)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
eigenvector (or eigenvector\_centrality)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
pagerank

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
clustering (or clustering\_coefficient)

\end{itemize}

\end{description}

\sphinxAtStartPar

\sphinxAtStartPar
Configure coverage filtering across groups.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Coverage determines which items appear in the final result based on
how many groups they appear in after grouping and top\_k filtering.
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Parameters}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{mode}} \textendash{} Coverage mode:
\sphinxhyphen{} “all”: Keep items that appear in ALL groups
\sphinxhyphen{} “any”: Keep items that appear in AT LEAST ONE group
\sphinxhyphen{} “at\_least”: Keep items that appear in at least k groups (requires k parameter)
\sphinxhyphen{} “exact”: Keep items that appear in exactly k groups (requires k parameter)
\sphinxhyphen{} “fraction”: Keep items that appear in at least p fraction (0\sphinxhyphen{}1) of groups (requires p parameter)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{k}} \textendash{} Threshold for “at\_least” or “exact” modes

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{p}} \textendash{} Fraction threshold (0.0\sphinxhyphen{}1.0) for “fraction” mode. E.g., p=0.67 means at least 67\% of groups

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{group}} \textendash{} Group attribute for coverage (defaults to primary grouping context)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{id\_field}} \textendash{} Field to use for identity matching (default: “id” for nodes)

\end{itemize}

\sphinxlineitem{Returns}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Self for chaining

\sphinxlineitem{Raises}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{ValueError}} \textendash{} If mode is invalid or required parameters are missing

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{ValueError}} \textendash{} If called without prior grouping

\end{itemize}

\end{description}\end{quote}

Aggregate over the current grouping context.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Computes summary statistics per group when grouping is active,
or globally if no grouping is set. Aggregation expressions are
strings like “mean(degree)”, “max(degree)”, “n()”.
\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Supported aggregations:}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
n() : count of items

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
mean(attr) : mean value

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
sum(attr) : sum of values

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
min(attr) : minimum value

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
max(attr) : maximum value

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
std(attr) : standard deviation

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
var(attr) : variance

\end{itemize}

\end{description}
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Parameters}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{**aggregations}} \textendash{} Named aggregations (name=expression)

\sphinxlineitem{Returns}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Self for chaining

\sphinxlineitem{Raises}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{ValueError}} \textendash{} If aggregation expression is invalid

\end{description}\end{quote}
\subsubsection*{Example}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{n}{Q}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{nodes}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{from\PYGZus{}layers}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{L}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{*}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{compute}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{degree}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{per\PYGZus{}layer}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{summarize}\PYG{p}{(}
\PYG{g+gp}{... }    \PYG{n}{mean\PYGZus{}degree}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{mean(degree)}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{g+gp}{... }    \PYG{n}{max\PYGZus{}degree}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{max(degree)}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{g+gp}{... }    \PYG{n}{n}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s+s2}{n()}\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}}
\PYG{g+gp}{... }\PYG{p}{)}

Decorator to register a Python function as a DSL operator.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This decorator allows users to define custom operators that can be used
in DSL queries. The decorated function should accept a DSLExecutionContext
as its first argument, followed by any keyword arguments.

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{description}} \textendash{} Human\sphinxhyphen{}readable description (defaults to function docstring)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{category}} \textendash{} Optional category for organization (e.g., “centrality”, “dynamics”)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{overwrite}} \textendash{} If True, allow replacing existing operators

Execute a DSL query on a multilayer network.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Supports both SELECT and MATCH queries:
\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{SELECT queries:}
\sphinxAtStartPar
SELECT nodes WHERE layer=”transport” AND degree \textgreater{} 5
SELECT * FROM nodes IN LAYER ‘ppi’ WHERE degree \textgreater{} 10
SELECT id, degree FROM nodes IN LAYERS (‘ppi’, ‘coexpr’) WHERE color = ‘red’

\sphinxlineitem{MATCH queries (Cypher\sphinxhyphen{}like):}
\sphinxAtStartPar
MATCH (g:Gene)\sphinxhyphen{}{[}r:REGULATES{]}\sphinxhyphen{}\textgreater{}(t:Gene) IN LAYER ‘reg’ WHERE g.degree \textgreater{} 10 RETURN g, t

\end{description}

\sphinxAtStartPar

\sphinxlineitem{Returns}

\sphinxAtStartPar

\subsubsection{Uncertainty Quantification}
\label{\detokenize{reference/api_index:module-py3plex.uncertainty}}\label{\detokenize{reference/api_index:uncertainty-quantification}}\index{module@\spxentry{module}!py3plex.uncertainty@\spxentry{py3plex.uncertainty}}\index{py3plex.uncertainty@\spxentry{py3plex.uncertainty}!module@\spxentry{module}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
First\sphinxhyphen{}class uncertainty support for py3plex.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This module provides types and utilities for representing statistics with
uncertainty information. The core idea is that every statistic is an object
that can carry a distribution:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Deterministic mode: object has mean with std=None (certainty 1.0)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Uncertainty mode: object has mean, std, quantiles populated

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
This makes uncertainty “first\sphinxhyphen{}class” \sphinxhyphen{} it’s baked into how numbers exist in
the library, not bolted on later.
\subsubsection*{Examples}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{py3plex}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{uncertainty}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{StatSeries}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Deterministic result}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{n}{result} \PYG{o}{=} \PYG{n}{StatSeries}\PYG{p}{(}
\PYG{g+gp}{... }    \PYG{n}{index}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{a}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{b}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{c}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{g+gp}{... }    \PYG{n}{mean}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{n}{np}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{array}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+m+mf}{1.0}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mf}{2.0}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mf}{3.0}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{g+gp}{... }\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{n}{result}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{is\PYGZus{}deterministic}
\PYG{g+go}{True}
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{n}{result}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{certainty}

\PYG{g+gp}{... }    \PYG{n}{index}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{a}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{b}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{l+s+s1}{c}\PYG{l+s+s1}{\PYGZsq{}}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{g+gp}{... }    \PYG{n}{mean}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{n}{np}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{array}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+m+mf}{1.0}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mf}{2.0}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mf}{3.0}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{,}
\PYG{g+gp}{... }    \PYG{n}{std}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{n}{np}\PYG{o}{.}\PYG{n}{array}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{p}{[}\PYG{l+m+mf}{0.1}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mf}{0.2}\PYG{p}{,} \PYG{l+m+mf}{0.15}\PYG{p}{]}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{,}

A series of statistics with optional uncertainty information.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This is the canonical result type for statistics that return a value per
node, time point, or other index.

\sphinxAtStartPar
In deterministic mode (uncertainty=False):
\sphinxhyphen{} mean contains the single\sphinxhyphen{}run values
\sphinxhyphen{} std = None
\sphinxhyphen{} quantiles = None
\sphinxhyphen{} certainty = 1.0

\sphinxAtStartPar
In uncertain mode (uncertainty=True):
\sphinxhyphen{} mean contains the average across runs
\sphinxhyphen{} std contains the standard deviation
\sphinxhyphen{} quantiles contains percentile arrays (e.g., \{0.025: arr, 0.975: arr\})
\sphinxhyphen{} certainty \textless{} 1.0

\sphinxAtStartPar
Estimate uncertainty for a network statistic.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This is the main entry point for adding uncertainty to any statistic.
It runs the metric function multiple times with different random seeds
or network perturbations, then computes mean, std, and quantiles.
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Parameters}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{network}} ({\hyperref[\detokenize{reference/api_index:py3plex.core.multinet.multi_layer_network}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{multi\_layer\_network}}}}}) \textendash{} The network to analyze.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{metric\_fn}} (\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{callable}}) \textendash{} Function that computes a statistic. Must accept a network and return:
\sphinxhyphen{} dict{[}node, float{]} for per\sphinxhyphen{}node statistics
\sphinxhyphen{} float for scalar statistics
\sphinxhyphen{} np.ndarray for array statistics

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{n\_runs}} (\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{int}}\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{, }}\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{optional}}) \textendash{} Number of runs for uncertainty estimation. If None, uses the
default from the current uncertainty config.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{resampling}} ({\hyperref[\detokenize{reference/api_index:py3plex.uncertainty.ResamplingStrategy}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{ResamplingStrategy}}}}}\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{, }}\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{optional}}) \textendash{} Strategy for resampling. If None, uses default from config.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{random\_seed}} (\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{int}}\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{, }}\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{optional}}) \textendash{} Random seed for reproducibility.

This is the canonical result type for statistics that return a value per

In deterministic mode (uncertainty=False):
\sphinxhyphen{} mean contains the single\sphinxhyphen{}run values
\sphinxhyphen{} std = None
\sphinxhyphen{} quantiles = None
\sphinxhyphen{} certainty = 1.0

In uncertain mode (uncertainty=True):
\sphinxhyphen{} mean contains the average across runs
\sphinxhyphen{} std contains the standard deviation
\sphinxhyphen{} quantiles contains percentile arrays (e.g., \{0.025: arr, 0.975: arr\})
\sphinxhyphen{} certainty \textless{} 1.0

\sphinxAtStartPar
Estimate uncertainty for a network statistic.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This is the main entry point for adding uncertainty to any statistic.
It runs the metric function multiple times with different random seeds
or network perturbations, then computes mean, std, and quantiles.
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Parameters}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{network}} ({\hyperref[\detokenize{reference/api_index:py3plex.core.multinet.multi_layer_network}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{multi\_layer\_network}}}}}) \textendash{} The network to analyze.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{metric\_fn}} (\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{callable}}) \textendash{} Function that computes a statistic. Must accept a network and return:
\sphinxhyphen{} dict{[}node, float{]} for per\sphinxhyphen{}node statistics
\sphinxhyphen{} float for scalar statistics
\sphinxhyphen{} np.ndarray for array statistics

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{n\_runs}} (\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{int}}\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{, }}\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{optional}}) \textendash{} Number of runs for uncertainty estimation. If None, uses the
default from the current uncertainty config.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{resampling}} ({\hyperref[\detokenize{reference/api_index:py3plex.uncertainty.ResamplingStrategy}]{\sphinxcrossref{\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{ResamplingStrategy}}}}}\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{, }}\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{optional}}) \textendash{} Strategy for resampling. If None, uses default from config.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{random\_seed}} (\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{int}}\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{, }}\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{optional}}) \textendash{} Random seed for reproducibility.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{perturbation\_params}} (\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{dict}}\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{, }}\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{optional}}) \textendash{} Parameters for perturbation strategies. For example:
\{“edge\_drop\_p”: 0.05, “node\_drop\_p”: 0.02\}

\end{itemize}

\sphinxlineitem{Returns}
\sphinxAtStartPar
If metric\_fn returns a dict: StatSeries with uncertainty info
If metric\_fn returns a scalar: float (mean value)
The returned object has mean, std, and quantiles populated.

{\hyperref[\detokenize{reference/api_index:py3plex.uncertainty.StatSeries}]{\sphinxcrossref{StatSeries}}} or float

\end{description}\end{quote}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Detect communities using the Infomap algorithm.
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Parameters}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{graph}} \textendash{} Input graph (NetworkX graph or multi\_layer\_network)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{binary}} \textendash{} Path to Infomap binary (default: “./infomap”)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{edgelist\_file}} \textendash{} Temporary file for edgelist (default: “./tmp/tmpedgelist.txt”)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{multiplex}} \textendash{} Whether to use multiplex mode (default: False)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{verbose}} \textendash{} Whether to show verbose output (default: False)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{overlapping}} \textendash{} Whether to detect overlapping communities (default: False)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{iterations}} \textendash{} Number of iterations (default: 200)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{output}} \textendash{} Output format \sphinxhyphen{} “mapping” or “partition” (default: “mapping”)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{seed}} \textendash{} Random seed for reproducibility (default: None)
Note: Requires Infomap binary that supports \textendash{}seed parameter

\end{itemize}

\sphinxlineitem{Returns}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Dict mapping nodes to community IDs (if output=”mapping”)
or Dict mapping community IDs to lists of nodes (if output=”partition”)

\sphinxlineitem{Raises}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{FileNotFoundError}} \textendash{} If Infomap binary is not found

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{PermissionError}} \textendash{} If Infomap binary is not executable

\end{itemize}

\end{description}\end{quote}

\index{module@\spxentry{module}!py3plex.algorithms.community\_detection.multilayer\_modularity@\spxentry{py3plex.algorithms.community\_detection.multilayer\_modularity}}\index{py3plex.algorithms.community\_detection.multilayer\_modularity@\spxentry{py3plex.algorithms.community\_detection.multilayer\_modularity}!module@\spxentry{module}}\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{reference/api_index:module-py3plex.algorithms.community_detection.multilayer_modularity}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Multilayer Modularity Maximization (Mucha et al., 2010)

\sphinxAtStartPar
This module implements multilayer modularity quality function and optimization
algorithms for community detection in multilayer/multiplex networks.
\subsubsection*{References}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Mucha et al., “Community Structure in Time\sphinxhyphen{}Dependent, Multiscale, and Multiplex
Networks”, Science 328:876\sphinxhyphen{}878 (2010)

\sphinxAtStartPar
Build the supra\sphinxhyphen{}modularity matrix B for multilayer network.

\sphinxAtStartPar
The supra\sphinxhyphen{}modularity matrix is:
B\_\{iα,jβ\} = (A\textasciicircum{}{[}α{]}\_ij \sphinxhyphen{} γ\textasciicircum{}{[}α{]} k\_i\textasciicircum{}α k\_j\textasciicircum{}α / 2m\_α) δ\_αβ + δ\_ij ω\_αβ

\sphinxAtStartPar
This matrix can be used for spectral community detection methods.
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Parameters}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{network}} \textendash{} py3plex multi\_layer\_network object

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{gamma}} \textendash{} Resolution parameter(s)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{omega}} \textendash{} Inter\sphinxhyphen{}layer coupling strength

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{weight}} \textendash{} Edge weight attribute

\end{itemize}

\sphinxlineitem{Returns}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Tuple of (modularity\_matrix, node\_layer\_list)
\sphinxhyphen{} modularity\_matrix: Supra\sphinxhyphen{}modularity matrix B (NL × NL)
\sphinxhyphen{} node\_layer\_list: List of (node, layer) tuples corresponding to matrix indices

\end{description}\end{quote}

\end{fulllineitems}\end{savenotes}

\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Generalized Louvain algorithm for multilayer networks.

\sphinxAtStartPar
This implements the multilayer Louvain method as described in Mucha et al. (2010),
which greedily maximizes the multilayer modularity quality function.
\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Complexity:}\begin{itemize}
\item {} \begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Time: O(n × L × d × k) per iteration, where:}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
n = number of nodes per layer

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
L = number of layers

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
d = average degree

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
k = number of communities

\end{itemize}

\end{description}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Typical: O(n × L) iterations until convergence

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Worst case: O((n×L)\(\sp{\text{2}}\)) for dense networks

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Space: O((n×L)\(\sp{\text{2}}\)) for supra\sphinxhyphen{}adjacency matrix (use sparse for large networks)

\end{itemize}

\end{description}
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Parameters}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{network}} \textendash{} py3plex multi\_layer\_network object

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{gamma}} \textendash{} Resolution parameter(s)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{omega}} \textendash{} Inter\sphinxhyphen{}layer coupling strength

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{weight}} \textendash{} Edge weight attribute

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{max\_iter}} \textendash{} Maximum number of iterations

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{random\_state}} \textendash{} Random seed for reproducibility

\end{itemize}

\sphinxlineitem{Returns}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Dictionary mapping (node, layer) tuples to community IDs

\end{description}\end{quote}
\subsubsection*{Examples}

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{g+gp}{\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{}\PYGZgt{} }\PYG{k+kn}{from}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nn}{py3plex}\PYG{n+nn}{.}\PYG{n+nn}{core}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k+kn}{import} \PYG{n}{multinet}

{{ $\rightarrow$ float}}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Calculate multilayer modularity quality function (Mucha et al., 2010).

\sphinxAtStartPar
The multilayer modularity is defined as:
Q = (1/2μ) Σ\_\{ijαβ\} {[}(A\textasciicircum{}{[}α{]}\_ij \sphinxhyphen{} γ\textasciicircum{}{[}α{]}P\textasciicircum{}{[}α{]}\_ij)δ\_αβ + δ\_ij ω\_αβ{]} δ(g\_iα, g\_jβ)

\sphinxAtStartPar
where:
\sphinxhyphen{} A\textasciicircum{}{[}α{]}\_ij is the adjacency matrix of layer α
\sphinxhyphen{} P\textasciicircum{}{[}α{]}\_ij is the null model (e.g., Newman\sphinxhyphen{}Girvan: k\_i\textasciicircum{}α k\_j\textasciicircum{}α / 2m\_α)
\sphinxhyphen{} γ\textasciicircum{}{[}α{]} is the resolution parameter for layer α
\sphinxhyphen{} ω\_αβ is the inter\sphinxhyphen{}layer coupling strength
\sphinxhyphen{} δ\_αβ = 1 if α=β, else 0 (Kronecker delta)
\sphinxhyphen{} δ\_ij = 1 if i=j, else 0
\sphinxhyphen{} δ(g\_iα, g\_jβ) = 1 if node i in layer α and node j in layer β are in same community
\sphinxhyphen{} μ is the total edge weight in the supra\sphinxhyphen{}network
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Parameters}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{network}} \textendash{} py3plex multi\_layer\_network object

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{communities}} \textendash{} Dictionary mapping (node, layer) tuples to community IDs

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{gamma}} \textendash{} Resolution parameter(s). Can be:
\sphinxhyphen{} Single float: same resolution for all layers
\sphinxhyphen{} Dict{[}layer, float{]}: layer\sphinxhyphen{}specific resolution parameters

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{omega}} \textendash{} Inter\sphinxhyphen{}layer coupling strength. Can be:
\sphinxhyphen{} Single float: uniform coupling between all layer pairs
\sphinxhyphen{} np.ndarray: layer\sphinxhyphen{}pair specific coupling matrix (L×L)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{weight}} \textendash{} Edge weight attribute (default: “weight”)

\end{itemize}

\sphinxlineitem{Returns}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Modularity value Q ∈ {[}\sphinxhyphen{}1, 1{]}

\end{description}\end{quote}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Compute the partition of the graph nodes which maximises the modularity
(or try..) using the Louvain heuristices

\sphinxAtStartPar
This is the partition of highest modularity, i.e. the highest partition
of the dendrogram generated by the Louvain algorithm.
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Parameters}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{graph}} (\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{networkx.Graph}}) \textendash{} the networkx graph which is decomposed

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{partition}} (\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{dict}}\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{, }}\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{optional}}) \textendash{} the algorithm will start using this partition of the nodes.
It’s a dictionary where keys are their nodes and values the communities

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{weight}} (\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{str}}\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{, }}\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{optional}}) \textendash{} the key in graph to use as weight. Default to ‘weight’

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{resolution}} (\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{double}}\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{, }}\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{optional}}) \textendash{} Will change the size of the communities, default to 1.
represents the time described in
“Laplacian Dynamics and Multiscale Modular Structure in Networks”,

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar

order to get different partitions at each call

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Find communities in the graph and return the associated dendrogram

\sphinxAtStartPar
A dendrogram is a tree and each level is a partition of the graph nodes.
Level 0 is the first partition, which contains the smallest communities,
and the best is len(dendrogram) \sphinxhyphen{} 1. The higher the level is, the bigger
are the communities
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Parameters}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{graph}} (\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{networkx.Graph}}) \textendash{} the networkx graph which will be decomposed

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{part\_init}} (\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{dict}}\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{, }}\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{optional}}) \textendash{} the algorithm will start using this partition of the nodes. It’s a
dictionary where keys are their nodes and values the communities

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{weight}} (\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{str}}\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{, }}\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{optional}}) \textendash{} the key in graph to use as weight. Default to ‘weight’

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{resolution}} (\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{double}}\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{, }}\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{optional}}) \textendash{} Will change the size of the communities, default to 1.
represents the time described in
“Laplacian Dynamics and Multiscale Modular Structure in Networks”,
R. Lambiotte, J.\sphinxhyphen{}C. Delvenne, M. Barahona

\end{itemize}

\sphinxlineitem{Returns}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{dendrogram} \textendash{} a list of partitions, ie dictionnaries where keys of the i+1 are the
values of the i. and where keys of the first are the nodes of graph

\sphinxlineitem{Return type}
\sphinxAtStartPar
list of dictionaries

\sphinxlineitem{Raises}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{TypeError}} \textendash{} If the graph is not a networkx.Graph

\end{description}\end{quote}

float

structure in networks. Physical Review E 69, 26113(2004).

{\sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{dendrogram}\DUrole{p}{:}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{n}{List\DUrole{p}{{[}}Dict\DUrole{p}{{]}}}}\sphinxparamcomma \sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{level}\DUrole{p}{:}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{n}{int}}}
{{ $\rightarrow$ Dict}}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Return the partition of the nodes at the given level

\sphinxAtStartPar
A dendrogram is a tree and each level is a partition of the graph nodes.
Level 0 is the first partition, which contains the smallest communities,
and the best is len(dendrogram) \sphinxhyphen{} 1.
The higher the level is, the bigger are the communities
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Parameters}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{dendrogram}} (\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{list}}\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{ of }}\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{dict}}) \textendash{} a list of partitions, ie dictionnaries where keys of the i+1 are the
values of the i.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{level}} (\sphinxstyleliteralemphasis{\sphinxupquote{int}}) \textendash{} the level which belongs to {[}0..len(dendrogram)\sphinxhyphen{}1{]}

\end{itemize}

\sphinxlineitem{Returns}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{partition} \textendash{} A dictionary where keys are the nodes and the values are the set it
belongs to

\sphinxlineitem{Return type}
\sphinxAtStartPar
dictionnary

\sphinxlineitem{Raises}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{KeyError}} \textendash{} If the dendrogram is not well formed or the level is too high

\end{description}\end{quote}

partitions in networks, including modularity, size distribution, and other
statistical metrics.

\index{module@\spxentry{module}!py3plex.algorithms.community\_detection.multilayer\_benchmark@\spxentry{py3plex.algorithms.community\_detection.multilayer\_benchmark}}\index{py3plex.algorithms.community\_detection.multilayer\_benchmark@\spxentry{py3plex.algorithms.community\_detection.multilayer\_benchmark}!module@\spxentry{module}}\phantomsection\label{\detokenize{reference/api_index:module-py3plex.algorithms.community_detection.multilayer_benchmark}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Multilayer Synthetic Graph Generation for Community Detection Benchmarks

\sphinxAtStartPar
This module implements synthetic multilayer/multiplex graph generators with
ground\sphinxhyphen{}truth community structure for benchmarking community detection algorithms.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Includes:
\sphinxhyphen{} Multilayer LFR (Lancichinetti\sphinxhyphen{}Fortunato\sphinxhyphen{}Radicchi) benchmark
\sphinxhyphen{} Coupled/Interdependent Erdős\sphinxhyphen{}Rényi models
\sphinxhyphen{} Support for overlapping communities across layers
\sphinxhyphen{} Support for partial node presence across layers
\subsubsection*{References}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Lancichinetti et al., “Benchmark graphs for testing community detection
algorithms”, Phys. Rev. E 78, 046110 (2008)

\sphinxAtStartPar
Granell et al., “Benchmark model to assess community structure in evolving
networks”, Phys. Rev. E 92, 012805 (2015)
\index{generate\_coupled\_er\_multilayer() (in module py3plex.algorithms.community\_detection.multilayer\_benchmark)@\spxentry{generate\_coupled\_er\_multilayer()}\spxextra{in module py3plex.algorithms.community\_detection.multilayer\_benchmark}}

{{ $\rightarrow$ Any}}
\pysigstopsignatures
\sphinxAtStartPar
Generate coupled/interdependent Erdős\sphinxhyphen{}Rényi multilayer networks.

\sphinxAtStartPar
Creates random Erdős\sphinxhyphen{}Rényi graphs in each layer and couples nodes across
layers with specified coupling strength and probability.
\begin{quote}\begin{description}
\sphinxlineitem{Parameters}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{n}} \textendash{} Number of nodes

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{layers}} \textendash{} List of layer names

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{p}} \textendash{} Edge probability per layer.
Can be float (same for all layers) or list of floats per layer.

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{omega}} \textendash{} Inter\sphinxhyphen{}layer coupling strength (weight of identity links)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{coupling\_probability}} \textendash{} Probability that a node has inter\sphinxhyphen{}layer coupling.
Range: {[}0, 1{]}
\sphinxhyphen{} 1.0 = all nodes coupled (full multiplex)
\sphinxhyphen{} \textless{}1.0 = partial coupling (interdependent networks)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{directed}} \textendash{} Whether to generate directed networks

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstyleliteralstrong{\sphinxupquote{seed}} \textendash{} Random seed for reproducibility

\end{itemize}

\sphinxlineitem{Returns}
\sphinxAtStartPar
py3plex multi\_layer\_network object

\end{description}\end{quote}
\subsubsection*{Examples}

\PYG{g+gp}{... }    \PYG{n}{p}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mf}{0.1}\PYG{p}{,}

\PYG{g+gp}{... }    \PYG{n}{coupling\PYGZus{}probability}\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{l+m+mf}{1.0}
\PYG{g+gp}{... }\PYG{p}{)}

}\DUrole{default_value}{False}}\sphinxparamcomma \sphinxparam{\DUrole{n}{seed}\DUrole{p}{:}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{n}{int\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{p}{|}\DUrole{w}{ }None}\DUrole{w}{ }\DUrole{o}{=}\DUrole{w}{
